FRACTAL ACADEMICS

The recent developments in the subject areas along with the innovation in Course structuring like ‘Fractal Academics’ and ‘Skill Orientation’ were incorporated in the Curriculum design in IIIT Naya Raipur. The innovative idea of ‘Fractal Academics’ though originated from Carnegie Melon University USA is being implemented in some of the new IITs in India as well.

IIIT NR has embedded issues like ‘Job-Orientation’ and ‘Research Enabling' as the driving force behind the Curriculum development, while encouraging the entrepreneurial instinct in the students.

The IIITNR Senate proposed a design of such curriculum which while making students Industry ready, also enables them to get into “Undergraduate Researching”. It is being endeavored to encourage the students in their Minor and Major project work to undertake research-oriented problems so that they may get exposed to many of the prevailing Science and Technology problems while supporting Faculty members in their Project/Research work as well.

exposed to many of the prevailing Science and Technology problems while supporting Faculty members in their Project/Research work as well.

Fractal academic supports to offer a course with less credit, minimum of one credit instead of courses with large credit in conventional curriculum system. This smaller credit subject is very useful to introduce industry related emerging subject. It facilitates T-Education model for both breadth and depth of knowledge.

The academics at IlIT Naya Raipur provides an optimum mixture of academics, research, and industry. We are always eager to learn and try to incorporate new things in our flexible curriculum.

The salient features of the Curriculum of IlITNR are:

Skill First, Theory Later, Projects Integrated

Fractal Academics, that enables offering of courses with smaller credits Learning by Doing Model

Fosters project-based learning

Exposure to both hardware + software in IT Workshops

Allows learning by application of theory

Enables development of both professional skills + technical skills Fosters interdisciplinary skills and wider knowledge enrichment Enables to cope up with fast changing IT revolution

Facilitates T-Education model for both breadth and depth of knowledge Engineering courses right from First semester instead of 12th ++ courses in First year

High Industry-linkages

B.TECH CURRICULUM

DSPM-IIITNR currently runs three undergraduate programs: B.Tech. in Computer Science & Engineering (CSE) , B.Tech. in Electronics & Communication Engineering (ECE) and BTech. in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DSAI) . These credit-based programs are designed to foster core skills with innovation and entrepreneurship skills among students. The dynamic structure of the curriculum orchestrates with the changing needs of industry and academia. IlIT Naya Raipur follows the Fractal Curriculum.

M.TECH CURRICULUM

M.Tech. program of the Institute is open to all Indian Nationals in the following specializations: Computer Science and Engineering (Intake :20 seats) Specializations: (a) Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (b) Information Security Electronics and Communication Engineering (Intake :20 seats) Specializations: (a) Communication and Signal Processing (b) VLSI and Embedded System

Some key features of M. Tech. program in IlIT-NR are listed below.

IIT-NR is mentored by a highly eminent board consisting of Mr. Ajai Chowdhry (Founder-HCL), Prof. Arogyaswami Paulraj (Marconi Award winner & Professor Emeritus-Stanford University) and other visionaries from Academia and Industry.

IIIT-NR is committed to bringing to the Institute the best of the faculty and resources to enable students create solutions for today's problems and products for the needs of the country, esp. the underprivileged.

Admissions in M.Tech. program is strictly based on valid GATE score. Eligible Applicants admitted to M.Tech. programme will receive a monthly Institute scholarship of Rs.12,400/-.

Students are encouraged to present research papers at reputed conferences and for which the institute supports financially as per the norms of IIIT Naya Raipur.

One Semester research abroad with institute financial assistantship up to 5 Lakhs for selected candidates.

PH.D

IIT Naya Raipur offers admission to the Ph.D. Programs in CSE, ECE,DSAI, Physics, Mathematics and Humanities. The goal of the Ph.D. program at llIT-NR is to prepare the scholars for becoming global academic, industrial and R\&D leaders.

Some key features of Ph.D. program in IlIT-NR are listed below.

IIIT-NR emphasizes to align its R\&D focus to achieve the goal of technological self-reliance. Faculties and research scholars conduct

research projects in several emerging areas of engineering, Science & Technology, and Management etc. The institute has ongoing < academic and research collaborations with many national and international universities, governments and industries in order to keep pace with expanding frontiers of knowledge and global developments.

Research scholars are encouraged to propose product or service based ideas useful to society and are encouraged to build working prototypes of these products. The institute involves exploration of some of the impacts of new technologies on society, usually the < unprivileged ones. privilegs

Research scholars admitted to Ph.D. program under regular Institute Scholar scheme (full time) are eligible for the Institute Teaching/Research Assistantship.

Research scholars are encouraged to present research papers at reputed conferences and attend eminent workshops in their respective research area. For this, the institute supports financially as per the norms of IlIT Naya Raipur.

About IIIT-NR Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee International Institute of Information Technology, Naya Raipur (IIIT-NR) is a premier state-funded institute established in 2015 under the International Institute of Information Technology University Act, 2013 of the Government of Chhattisgarh. The institute is a joint initiative of the Government of Chhattisgarh and National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) Limited, a Maharatna Central Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Power, Government of India. Incorporated as a state university and recognized by the University Grants Commission (UGC) and approved by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), IIIT-NR is committed to pursuing excellence in higher education, research, and development in Information Technology (IT) and associated disciplines. The institute firmly believes in knowledge dissemination and in imparting entrepreneurial skills to its students, enabling them to address real-world problems with confidence and creativity. The institute is housed on a fully residential, fifty-acre green campus in Naya Raipur (Atal Nagar) — India's first planned green and smart city — approximately 23 km from Raipur and well connected by air, rail, and road. The serene environment blends natural beauty with state-of-the-art infrastructure, creating an ideal space for innovation and learning. IIIT-NR offers

natural beauty with state-of-the-art infrastructure, creating an ideal space for innovation and learning. IIIT-NR offers undergraduate (B.Tech.), postgraduate (M.Tech.), and doctoral (Ph.D.) programmes in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE), Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE), and Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DSAI). These credit-based programmes are designed to foster core competence together with innovation and entrepreneurship, with a dynamic curriculum structure that keeps pace with the changing needs of industry and academia. Vision of the Institute To be a globally recognized institution of excellence in information technology and allied disciplines, nurturing innovators, entrepreneurs, and socially responsible technologists who contribute to national and global development. Mission of the Institute • To impart high-quality, value-based, and outcome-oriented technical education. • To foster state-of-the-art, interdisciplinary research and product development. • To cultivate entrepreneurial mind-sets and industry-ready professional skills. • To engage with society and industry for sustainable and inclusive growth. B.Tech CSE Syllabus • Dr. SPM IIIT-NR 2. About the Department of CSE The Department of Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) at IIIT-NR offers a four-year Bachelor of Technology programme that builds a strong foundation in the theory and practice of computing — spanning programming, data structures and algorithms, systems, databases, networks, and the rapidly growing areas of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data science. The programme combines rigorous fundamentals with extensive hands-on laboratory work, design projects, and industry-aligned skills so that graduates are equipped to design, build, and reason about complex software and computing systems. The department is taught by highly qualified and research-active faculty whose expertise spans artificial intelligence and machine learning, data science, computer networks and security, distributed and cloud systems, theoretical computer science, computer vision, and software engineering. Every semester integrates project-based learning, supported by well-equipped computing laboratories, high-performance computing resources, and the active mentorship of research scholars. AI-assisted full-stack prototyping is embedded from the first year, reflecting the institute's emphasis on innovation and entrepreneurship. Vision of the Department To emerge as a centre of excellence in computer science and engineering

of the Department To emerge as a centre of excellence in computer science and engineering education and research, producing globally competent engineers, innovators, and entrepreneurs capable of solving complex computing problems for the benefit of society. Mission of the Department

1. To provide a rigorous, outcome-based foundation in computer science and engineering with strong hands-on, design, and problem-solving exposure. 2. To promote research, innovation, and entrepreneurship in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence, data science, cyber-security, and distributed and intelligent systems. 3. To inculcate professional ethics, lifelong learning, and social responsibility among students. 4. To build strong linkages with industry, research organizations, and the wider community for mutually beneficial collaboration. Programme Offered B.Tech. in Computer Science and Engineering — 4 years / 8 semesters, 160 credits, with multiple entry- exit options, multidisciplinary minors, an Honors track, and a strong project and internship component, in line with NEP 2020 and the NBA outcome-based education framework. CO2 Carry out matrix operations including inverses, rank, and determinants. CO3 Determine eigenvalues and eigenvectors and solve eigenvalue problems. CO4 Apply matrix algebra to linear transformations and change of basis. CO5 Demonstrate understanding of inner-product spaces, orthonormalization, and SVD. Detailed Syllabus (5 Modules) Mod. Vector Spaces M2 Vector spaces over real and complex fields; subspaces; linear dependence and 6 independence; spanning set; basis and dimension. Linear Transformations M3 Linear transformations and their matrices; kernel and range; change of basis; rank- 6 nullity theorem; matrix representation. A. NSS (Hours of Service): NSS Coordinator will be responsible for providing the grade Grade A+ A B+ B C+ C F Hours of ≥ 240 200-239 180-199 140-179 100-139 60-99 <60 service B. ISR (30 Activities in Two years): ISR Coordinator will be responsible for providing the grade Grade A+ A B+ B C+ C F Present ≥ 90% 80%- 70%- 60%- 50%- 40%- <40% in % of 89% 79% 69% 59% 49% activities a. Students can attend any one activity to earn the grade. b. If a student wants to increase their grade, they need to participate in another activity also. Then the final grade will be decided by combining the grades of the two activities (NSS and ISR). For example, If a student scores an A in NSS and a C in ISR, his final grade will be A+. In general, students will be given one grade above the maximum grade of two activities, provided both grades are C and above. c. For an F grade, the student has to do all ISR activities in the next semester.

Co-curricular & Extra-curricular Activities Students' participation in the institute activities up to IV sem a. Different clubs: technical and non-technical clubs; the coordinator of clubs will provide the names of students with attendance in the number of sessions and achievements b. Sports activities: participation in institute sports activities and sports competition: The SAC president will be responsible for providing the participant's name c. Attend IEEE activities and institute talk: The IEEE Coordinator will be responsible for providing the name d. Volunteers in different technical and non-technical events. The faculty coordinator of particular activities will be responsible for providing the participant's name. All activities will have equal weightage. About IIIT-NR Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee International Institute of Information Technology, Naya Raipur (IIIT-NR) is a premier state-funded institute established in 2015 under the International Institute of Information Technology University Act, 2013 of the Government of Chhattisgarh. The institute is a joint initiative of the Government of Chhattisgarh and National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) Limited, a Maharatna Central Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Power, Government of India. Incorporated as a state university and recognized by the University Grants Commission (UGC) and approved by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), IIIT-NR is committed to pursuing excellence in higher education, research, and development in Information Technology (IT) and associated disciplines. The institute firmly believes in knowledge dissemination and in imparting entrepreneurial skills to its students, enabling them to address real-world problems with confidence and creativity. The institute is housed on a fully residential, fifty-acre green campus in Naya Raipur (Atal Nagar) — India's first planned green and smart city — approximately 23 km from Raipur and well connected by air, rail, and road. The serene environment blends natural beauty with state-of-the-art infrastructure, creating an ideal space for innovation

The serene environment blends natural beauty with state-of-the-art infrastructure, creating an ideal space for innovation and learning. IIIT-NR offers undergraduate (B.Tech.), postgraduate (M.Tech.), and doctoral (Ph.D.) programmes in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE), Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE), and Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DSAI). These credit-based programmes are designed to foster core competence together with innovation and entrepreneurship, with a dynamic curriculum structure that keeps pace with the changing needs of industry and academia. Vision of the Institute To be a globally recognized institution of excellence in information technology and allied disciplines, nurturing innovators, entrepreneurs, and socially responsible technologists who contribute to national and global development. Mission of the Institute • To impart high-quality, value-based, and outcome-oriented technical education. • To foster state-of-the-art, interdisciplinary research and product development. • To cultivate entrepreneurial mind-sets and industry-ready professional skills. • To engage with society and industry for sustainable and inclusive growth. About the Department of DSAI The Department of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DSAI) at IIIT-NR offers a four-year Bachelor of Technology programme that builds a strong foundation in computing and then develops deep specialization in data science, artificial intelligence, and machine learning. Alongside a solid core of programming, data structures, algorithms, databases, and systems, the programme provides rigorous training in statistics, optimization, machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, natural-language processing, reinforcement learning, and the emerging areas of generative and agentic AI. The curriculum combines mathematical depth with extensive hands-on practice so that graduates can design, build, and reason about intelligent, data-driven systems. The department is taught by highly qualified and research-active faculty whose expertise spans machine learning and deep learning, data science and analytics, computer vision, natural-language processing, reinforcement learning, statistical modelling, and trustworthy and responsible AI. Every semester integrates project-based learning, supported by well-equipped computing laboratories, GPU/high- performance computing resources, and the active mentorship of research scholars. AI-assisted full-stack prototyping is embedded from the first year, reflecting the

mentorship of research scholars. AI-assisted full-stack prototyping is embedded from the first year, reflecting the institute's emphasis on innovation and entrepreneurship. Vision of the Department To emerge as a centre of excellence in data science and artificial intelligence education and research, producing globally competent engineers, innovators, and entrepreneurs capable of building intelligent, data-driven, and responsible solutions for the benefit of society. Mission of the Department 1. To provide a rigorous, outcome-based foundation in data science and artificial intelligence with strong mathematical, computational, and hands-on exposure. 2. To promote research, innovation, and entrepreneurship in emerging areas such as deep learning, computer vision, natural-language processing, and generative and agentic AI. 3. To inculcate professional ethics, responsible-AI practices, lifelong learning, and social responsibility among students. 4. To build strong linkages with industry, research organizations, and the wider community for mutually beneficial collaboration. Prerequisite NIL Laboratory No Introduces students to the fundamental concepts of personal and corporate finance, building the financial literacy needed to make informed decisions about savings, investment, credit, and basic business finance. Course Outcomes (COs) On successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: CO Statement Explain core financial concepts, including the time value of money and interest

computation. CO2 Compare savings, investment, and insurance instruments based on risk and return. CO3 Apply budgeting and financial-planning principles to personal financial decisions. CO4 Interpret basic corporate financial statements and key financial ratios. Detailed Syllabus (5 Modules) Mod. Content Hours Foundations of Finance — Overview of the financial system and institutions; M1 time value of money; simple and compound interest; present value and future 5 value; inflation and purchasing power. Personal Finance & Investment — Savings and budgeting; banking and M2 digital payment systems; insurance basics; introduction to mutual funds and the 5 stock market; risk-return trade-off; retirement and tax planning basics. Corporate Finance Basics — Reading financial statements (balance sheet, M3 P&L, cash flow); key financial ratios; sources of business finance (equity, debt); 4 basics of capital budgeting. Then the final grade will be decided by combining the grades of the two activities (NSS and ISR). For example, If a student scores an A in NSS and a C in ISR, his final grade will be A+. B.Tech ECE Syllabus • Dr. SPM IIIT-NR 1. About IIIT-NR Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee International Institute of Information Technology, Naya Raipur (IIIT-NR) is a premier state-funded institute established in 2015 under the International Institute of Information Technology University Act, 2013 of the Government of Chhattisgarh. The institute is a joint initiative of the Government of Chhattisgarh and National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) Limited, a Maharatna Central Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Power, Government of India. Incorporated as a state university and recognized by the University Grants Commission (UGC) and approved by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), IIIT-NR is committed to pursuing excellence in higher education, research, and development in Information Technology (IT) and associated disciplines. The institute firmly believes in knowledge dissemination and in imparting entrepreneurial skills to its students, enabling them to address real-world problems with confidence and creativity. The institute is housed on a fully residential, fifty-acre green campus in Naya Raipur (Atal Nagar) — India's first planned green and smart city — approximately 23 km from Raipur and well connected by air, rail, and road. The serene environment blends natural beauty with state-of-the-art infrastructure, creating an ideal space for innovation

The serene environment blends natural beauty with state-of-the-art infrastructure, creating an ideal space for innovation and learning. IIIT-NR offers undergraduate (B.Tech.), postgraduate (M.Tech.), and doctoral (Ph.D.) programmes in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE), Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE), and Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DSAI). These credit-based programmes are designed to foster core competence together with innovation and entrepreneurship, with a dynamic curriculum structure that keeps pace with the changing needs of industry and academia. Vision of the Institute To be a globally recognized institution of excellence in information technology and allied disciplines, nurturing innovators, entrepreneurs, and socially responsible technologists who contribute to national and global development. Mission of the Institute • To impart high-quality, value-based, and outcome-oriented technical education. • To foster state-of-the-art, interdisciplinary research and product development. • To cultivate entrepreneurial mind-sets and industry-ready professional skills. • To engage with society and industry for sustainable and inclusive growth. B.Tech ECE Syllabus • Dr. SPM IIIT-NR 2. About the Department of ECE The Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE) at IIIT-NR offers a four-year Bachelor of Technology programme that provides a strong conceptual foundation in electronics, communication, signal processing, and VLSI, complemented by intensive hands-on experience in designing and building electronic hardware and embedded systems. The programme has been developed in response to the evolving needs of industry, equipping students with advanced knowledge and skills for the design of complex electronic and communication systems. The department is taught by highly qualified and research-active faculty whose expertise spans wireless and next-generation communications (5G/6G, OTFS, UAV networks), VLSI and microelectronics, embedded and IoT systems, RF and microwave engineering, signal processing, control, and machine learning for communications. Every semester integrates project work that combines coding and electronics skills, supported by well-equipped laboratories and the active mentorship of research scholars. Vision of the Department To emerge as a centre of excellence in electronics and communication engineering education and research, producing globally competent engineers and innovators capable of addressing the technological challenges of a connected world. Mission of the Department 1. To

of addressing the technological challenges of a connected world. Mission of the Department 1. To provide a rigorous, outcome-based foundation in electronics and communication engineering with strong hands-on and design exposure. 2. To promote research, innovation, and entrepreneurship in emerging areas such as next-generation wireless, VLSI, embedded systems, and intelligent electronics. 3. To inculcate professional ethics, lifelong learning, and social responsibility among students. 4. To build strong linkages with industry, research organizations, and the wider community for mutually beneficial collaboration. Programme Offered B.Tech. in Electronics and Communication Engineering — 4 years / 8 semesters, 160 credits, with multiple entry-exit options, multidisciplinary minors, an Honors track, and a strong project and internship component, in line with NEP 2020 and the NBA outcome-based education framework. (ECE) curriculum is designed and delivered following the Outcome-Based Education (OBE) philosophy advocated by the National Board of Accreditation (NBA) and consistent with the Washington Accord. Prerequisite Nil Laboratory No Provides the matrix-algebraic and vector-space foundation underpinning signal processing, communications, control, machine learning, and numerical computation in electronics engineering. Course Outcomes (COs) On successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: CO Statement CO1 Solve systems of linear equations using Gaussian elimination and matrix inversion. CO2 Carry out matrix operations including inverses, rank, and determinants. CO3 Determine eigenvalues and eigenvectors and solve eigenvalue problems. CO4 Apply matrix algebra to linear transformations and change of basis. CO5 Demonstrate understanding of inner-product spaces, orthonormalization, and SVD. Detailed Syllabus (5 Modules) Mod. Linear Transformations M3 Linear transformations and their matrices; kernel and range; change of basis; rank- 6 nullity theorem; matrix representation. A. NSS (Hours of Service): NSS Coordinator will be responsible for providing the grade Grade A+ A B+ B C+ C F Hours of ≥ 240 200-239 180-199 140-179 100-139 60-99 <60 service B. ISR (30 Activities in Two years): ISR Coordinator will be responsible for providing the grade Grade A+ A B+ B C+ C F Present ≥ 90% 80%- 70%- 60%- 50%- 40%- <40% in % of 89% 79% 69% 59% 49% activities a. Students can attend any one activity to earn the grade. b. If a student wants to increase their grade, they need to participate in another activity also. Then the final grade will be decided by combining the grades of the two activities (NSS and ISR). For example, If a student scores an A in NSS and a C in ISR, his final grade will be A+. In general, students will be given one grade above the maximum grade of two activities, provided both grades are C and above. c. For an F grade, the student has to do all ISR activities in the next semester.

Different clubs: technical and non-technical clubs; the coordinator of clubs will provide the names of students with attendance in the number of sessions and achievements b. Sports activities: participation in institute sports activities and sports competition: The SAC president will be responsible for providing the participant's name c. Attend IEEE activities and institute talk: The IEEE Coordinator will be responsible for providing the name d. Volunteers in different technical and non-technical events. The faculty coordinator of particular activities will be responsible for providing the participant's name. All activities will have equal weightage. Course Title Linear Algebra & Matrix Analysis Course Code MA01 Department CSE/ECE/DSAI/SCI. & MATHS/HUMANITIES Credits, Structure ( L- 3, (2-1-0-0)

Offered for All Programs Type Compulsory Prerequisite NA Laboratory No Course Outcomes At the end of the course, students should be able to: 1. Solve systems of linear equations using multiple methods, including Gaussian elimination and matrix inversion. 2. Carry out matrix operations, including inverses and determinants. 3. Determine eigenvalues and eigenvectors and solve eigenvalue problems. 4. Apply principles of matrix algebra to linear transformations. 5. Demonstrate understanding of inner products and associated norms. Contents: System of linear equations, Inverse and rank of a matrix by using elementary transformations, Properties of determinants Vector space over real and complex fields, Linear dependence, independence and spanning set, Linear transformation and its matrix, Change of basis, Eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Diagonalization of matrices. Inner product spaces, Gram-Schmidt orthonormalization, Singular Value Decomposition (SVD). Text Books 1. Seymour Lipschutz, Marc Lipson, Schaum’s outlines of Linear Algebra ,McGraw-Hill Education 2. J. Defranza and D. Gagliardi, Introduction to Linear Algebra with Applications, McGraw-Hill 3. K. section_title: Course Title Calculus Course Code MA02
heading_path: Course Title Calculus Course Code MA02

text: Offered for All Programs Type Compulsory Prerequisite NA Laboratory No Course Outcomes At the end of the course, students should be able to: 1. Find limits of functions (graphically, numerically and algebraically) 2. Analyse and apply the notions of continuity and differentiability to algebraic and transcendental functions. 3. Determine derivatives using implicit differentiation and use to study characteristics of a curve. 4. Apply the Fundamental theorem of calculus to evaluate definite integrals. 5. Use differentiation and integration to solve real world problems such as rate of change, optimization, and area problems. Contents: Review of single variable calculus: Review of Limit, continuity and differentiability of single variable functions, Indeterminate forms and L’Hospital rule, Mean Value theorem, Maclaurin and Taylor series expansions of functions of one variable. Offered for All Programs Type Compulsory Prerequisite NA Laboratory Choice Mandatory Course Description: This hands-on workshop enables students to design, develop, and deploy end-to-end functional prototypes for web and mobile applications, leveraging AI-powered tools for faster development. The course blends Full Stack development (front-end, back-end, and database) with AI-assisted features such as code generation, UI design, data handling, and intelligent services. Course Outcomes (COs): On successful completion of this course, students will be able to:  CO1: Apply fundamental concepts of full stack development (frontend, backend, database, APIs) to design functional prototypes.  CO2: Use AI-assisted tools to accelerate coding, interface design, and backend logic development.  CO3: Integrate AI/ML services (e.g., Chatbots, Recommendation Engines, Vision APIs) into full stack prototypes.  CO4: Deploy prototypes to cloud platforms for public access.  CO5: Collaborate effectively in teams, managing workflows using modern DevOps tools and agile principles. Mapping to Graduate Attributes: Engineering knowledge, Problem Analysis, Design/Development, Modern Tool Usage, Ethics, Communication, and Project Management. Course Contents: Module 1 – Introduction & Tools Setup (Week 1) - Full Stack architecture overview (Client–Server–Database), AI- powered development tools: GitHub

Tools Setup (Week 1) - Full Stack architecture overview (Client–Server–Database), AI- powered development tools: GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Cursor, Replit, etc., Setting up environment: Node.js, Python/Flask/Django, React/Vue, VS Code, Git/GitHub Module 2 – Frontend Development with AI Assistance (Weeks 2–3) - HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript ES6+ basics (AI-assisted code snippets), Component-based UI design using React/Vue, Responsive design frameworks (Bootstrap/Tailwind CSS), AI-assisted prototyping for UI/UX Module 3 – Backend Development & APIs (Weeks 4–5) - REST API concepts and design, Backend frameworks: Express.js / Flask / Django, AI-assisted code scaffolding for CRUD operations, Authentication & authorization basics Module 4 – Databases & Integration (Week 6) - SQL (MySQL/PostgreSQL) and NoSQL (MongoDB), AI-assisted query generation and optimization, ORM integration (SQLAlchemy, Mongoose) Module 5 – AI/ML Service Integration (Weeks 7–8) - Integrating OpenAI, Hugging Face, or Google Cloud AI APIs, Adding chatbots, summarizers, sentiment analysis, or computer vision to prototypes, Data preprocessing using AI tools Module 6 – Deployment & DevOps Basics (Week 9) - Deploying applications using Vercel, Netlify, or Heroku, Containerization with Docker (optional), AI-assisted CI/CD setup Module 7 – Project Sprint & Demo Day (Weeks 10–12) - Agile project management tools,

Module 7 – Project Sprint & Demo Day (Weeks 10–12) - Agile project management tools, (Trello/Jira), Team sprints with AI-assisted task completion, Final demo and peer evaluation Course Projects (Examples): Students will work in teams to develop one full stack prototype with AI-assisted features. Possible project ideas include: 1. AI-Powered Resume Builder – Generates resumes using user input, with real-time formatting and download options. 2. E-Commerce Portal with AI Recommendations – AI-based product suggestions and chatbot support. 3. Smart Student Portal – With AI-assisted assignment summaries and automated FAQs. 4. Travel Itinerary Planner – AI-generated itineraries based on preferences, with map integration. 5. Healthcare Symptom Checker – Uses NLP models to provide probable condition information. Text Books: 1. Srinivasa K G, et al., AI-Assisted Programming for Web and Machine Learning, BPB Publishers, 2025. 2. Bates, B., & Downey, C., Programming with AI Tools: A Developer’s Guide, Manning Publications. text: Offered for All Programs Type Compulsory Prerequisite Sensors & Actuators Laboratory Choice Mandatory Course Outcomes At the end of the course, students should be able to: 1. Understand the basic concepts of different measurement & Mechatronics systems, the function, suitability of different Sensors and Actuators and understand in depth the concepts of Input/Output Signal conditioning 2. Understand the Architectural Overview of IoT and Real World Design Constraints 3. Implement interfacing of various sensors with Arduino/Node MCU, Raspberry Pi, etc. 4. section_title: Course Title Quantum Mechanics Course Code SC01
heading_path: Course Title Quantum Mechanics Course Code SC01

text: Offered for All Programs Type Compulsory Prerequisite NA Laboratory Choice Faculty Choice Course Outcomes At the end of the course, students should be able to: 1. Use with the language of basic quantum mechanics and formalism. 2. carry out calculations of atoms and molecules and describe quantum phenomenon within the electron physics from quantum mechanical relations. 3. carry out spectroscopic studies of different subjects and interpret the results in quantized units. 4. report on applications of quantum physics in nature, technical developments and society. Contents: Basics of Quantum Mechanics: Basic principles of quantum mechanics, wave function and the uncertainty principle, probability wave amplitude, probability density, wave equation and Schrodinger formalism, time-independent and time-dependent Schrodinger equations, eigenstate and eigenvalues, expectation values. Wave Formalism of Quantum Mechanics: Schrodinger Equation in one dimension, and applications. Hydrogen Atom (Spherically symmetric potential) : Orbital and spin angular momentum operators, eigenstates and eigenvalues of angular momentum, central potential, solutions of Schrodinger equation in a central potential and applications (Hydrogen-like atom). Dirac’s bra and ket algebra: Introduction, bra and ket notation, angular momenta, Clebsch-Gordon coefficients, spin-orbit interaction and applications. Hilbert

section_title: Course Title Probability & Statistics Course Code MA03
heading_path: Course Title Probability & Statistics Course Code MA03

text: Offered for All Programs Type Compulsory Prerequisite NA Laboratory Choice Faculty Choice Course Outcomes At the end of the course, students should be able to: 1. Use the basic probability rules, including additive and multiplicative laws, using the terms, independent and mutually exclusive events. 2. Analyze statistical data using measures of central tendency, dispersion and location. 3. Identify the characteristics of different discrete and continuous distributions. 4. Translate real-world problems into probability models. 5. Identify the type of statistical situation to which different distributions can be applied. Contents: Axiomatic definition of probability, Probability on finite sample spaces, Joint and conditional probabilities, independence, total probability; Bayes’ rule and applications. section_title: Course Title Signals and Systems Course Code ECE02
heading_path: Course Title Signals and Systems Course Code ECE02

text: Offered for All Programs Type Compulsory Prerequisite NA Laboratory Choice Faculty Choice Course Outcomes At the end of the course, students should be able to: 1. Understand different types of signals-continuous and discrete, odd and even, periodic and aperiodic etc. 2. Classify systems based on their properties 3. Analyse continuous time signals and systems by using appropriate mathematical tools 4. Analyse sampling process and sampling of discrete time signals. 5. Determine Fourier transforms for continuous-time and discrete-time signals Contents: Signals: classification of signals; signal operations: scaling, shifting and inversion; signal properties; elementary signals. Systems: classification of systems; system properties; continuous-time linear time invariant (LTI) and discrete-time linear shift invariant (LSI) systems: impulse response and step response; response to an arbitrary input: convolution; system representation using differential and difference equations; Eigen functions of LTI systems, frequency response and its relation to the impulse response. Fourier series representation of continuous-time and discrete-time signals, continuous-time Fourier transform and its properties; Parseval’s relation, time-bandwidth product; discrete-time Fourier transform and its properties; relations among various Fourier representations, Time and Frequency characterization of

Fourier transform and its properties; relations among various Fourier representations, Time and Frequency characterization of Signals and Systems, DFT. Sampling theorem; aliasing; signal reconstruction: ideal interpolator, zero-order hold, first-order hold. Definition, region of convergence, properties; transform-domain analysis of LTI/LSI systems, system function: poles and zeros; stability. Text Books 1. A.V. Oppenheim, A.S. Willsky and H.S. section_title: Course Title Introduction to AI & ML Course Code DSAI01
heading_path: Course Title Introduction to AI & ML Course Code DSAI01

text: Offered for All Programs Type Compulsory Prerequisite Linear Algebra and Probability Laboratory Choice Mandatory Course Outcomes At the end of the course, students should be able to: 1. Understand how AI is different from machine learning 2. Appraise the underlying mathematical relationships within machine learning algorithms and the paradigms of supervised and unsupervised learning 3. Decide what kind of machine learning paradigm can be applied to solve the underlying real-world application 4. Distinguish a game situation from pure individual decision problem Course Objectives:  Introduce the fundamental concepts and applications of AI and ML in an intuitive, non-mathematical manner.  Familiarize students with AI/ML workflows and popular tools through real-world datasets and competitions.  Encourage curiosity and self-learning through open platforms like Kaggle, AIcrowd, and Google Colab. Proposed Lecture Plan (14 Hours):

1. Introduction to AI & ML History & evolution of AI; Difference between AI, ML, and DL; 2 Real-world applications in different sectors 2. Data and Problem Understanding datasets, features, labels; Types of ML problems 2 Formulation – classification, regression, clustering 3. ML Workflow Basics Data preprocessing, train/test split, model training, evaluation 2 metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1) 4. Core Algorithms (Intuitive) Linear regression, decision trees, k-NN, Naïve Bayes; Intro to 3 neural networks 5. AI Tools & Platforms Google Colab, Jupyter, Kaggle kernels & competitions, AIcrowd 2 6. Ethics & Responsible AI Bias in data, fairness, explainability, data privacy 1 7. Course Wrap-up & Problem statement release for class competition, expectations, 2 Competition Launch evaluation Practical & Competition-Based Learning: Students will work on at least two mini-projects/competitions during lab/practical sessions: 1. Beginner-level Kaggle Competition o Example: Titanic – Machine Learning from Disaster (binary classification) o Goal: Submit predictions, view leaderboard, learn iterative improvement. 2. Custom AI Challenge o Could be hosted internally or via AIcrowd/DrivenData. o Examples: Handwritten digit recognition (MNIST), basic sentiment analysis, house price prediction. 3. Open Exploration o Teams can optionally pick their own small dataset and apply ML pipeline

Open Exploration o Teams can optionally pick their own small dataset and apply ML pipeline steps. Tools & Resources:  Platforms: Kaggle, AIcrowd, DrivenData, Google Colab  Libraries: scikit-learn, pandas, matplotlib, seaborn, TensorFlow/PyTorch (basic exposure only)  Datasets: From competition portals or open datasets (UCI ML Repository, Kaggle Datasets) References: 1. Géron, A., Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O’Reilly. (select chapters for intuition) 2. Raschka, S., Python Machine Learning, Packt Publishing. (for self-learners) 3. Kaggle Learn Micro-Courses – https://www.kaggle.com/learn 4. AIcrowd Challenges – https://www.aicrowd.com/challenges 5. Google Colab – https://colab.research.google.com/ Page 16 of 21

text: Offered for All Programs Type Compulsory Prerequisite - Laboratory Choice Mandatory Course Objectives:  Provide an overview of the origin, structure, and key features of the Indian Constitution.  Create awareness of citizens’ rights, duties, and the role of governance.  Enable students to connect constitutional principles with technology, ethics, and society. Course Outcomes (COs): By the end of this course, students will be able to: CO1: Summarize the historical background and philosophy of the Constitution. CO2: Describe fundamental rights, duties, and directive principles. CO3: Identify the structure and functioning of the Union, State, and Local Governments. CO4: Relate constitutional provisions to technology, governance, and professional ethics. Lecture Plan (14 Hours)

Fundamental Rights Equality, Freedom, Constitutional Remedies 2 4. Directive Principles & Fundamental Purpose, examples, professional and civic relevance 2 Duties President, Prime Minister, Parliament, Governor, 5. Structure of Government 2 CM, Judiciary 6. Dipanjan Sar is a dedicated researcher specializing in wireless communication, AI/ML, Internet of Vehicles (IoV) communication, and waveform design. He is currently pursuing his Ph.D. in Electronics and Communication Engineering at IIIT Naya Raipur, alongside working as a Senior Research Fellow (SRF) in a National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS) funded project.

With a B.Tech in ECE from West Bengal University of Technology (WBUT) and an M.Tech from IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, he brings a strong academic foundation to his research. His work focuses on channel estimation and waveform design for the next-generation Internet of Vehicles (IoV).

Dipanjan has also contributed significantly to academia, having over three years of teaching experience at Techno India Banipur (WB) and Chaibasa Engineering College (Jharkhand). His expertise lies in bridging the gap between theoretical research and practical applications, driving innovation in wireless communication and intelligent vehicular networks.

Gopesh Kumar Bharti is a Junior Research Fellow (JRF) at IIIT Naya Raipur and a Ph.D. scholar in Computer Science and Engineering. His research is centered on developing an AI-based translation tool for converting English/Hindi text and speech to tribal languages, particularly Gondi, and vice versa. Leveraging transformer-based neural machine translation models, his work aims to enhance linguistic inclusivity and accessibility. He holds an M.Tech and B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering from Chhattisgarh Swami Vivekanand Technical University, Bhilai (C.G.). His research contributes to the preservation and promotion of indigenous languages through AI-driven language technologies.

Supervisor : Dr. Santosh Kumar

About IIIT Naya Raipur Dr Shyama Prasad Mukherjee IIIT-Naya Raipur (IIIT-NR), established by the International Institute of Information Technology University Act, 2013 of the Government of Chhattisgarh, is a joint initiative of the Chhattisgarh State Government and National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC). The institute is committed to pursuing excellence in higher education, research, and development in information technology (IT) and other associated disciplines. IIIT-NR firmly believes in bestowing knowledge dissemination and imparting entrepreneurial skills to the students to enable them to address real-world problems. To empower this vision, IIIT-NR provides state-of-the-art research and education facilities and nurtures a campus culture that fosters high energy and enthusiasm in every individual, clubbed with the highest standard of professionalism. Facilities: The 50 acres of the lush green campus of IIIT-NR is enabled with Wi-Fi connectivity and has excellent amenities for sports and other recreational activities. The modern architecture of the buildings and the serene environment of the campus foster an ambience for the students to engage in creativity and innovation.

<!-- page: 3 -->

The institute has two state-of-the-art virtual classrooms of 120 capacity each quipped with the latest video conferencing systems. The classrooms and laboratories are equipped with state-of-the-art tools for teaching and learning. Some important laboratories are the 3D Printing & Fabrication Lab, 5G Lab, Antenna and Microwave Circuit Design Lab, Big Data Computing Lab, VLSI & Embedded Lab, Artificial Intelligence & Deep Learning Lab, Communication Lab, Data Science Lab, IoT & Sensor Lab, Robotics Lab, etc. IIIT-NR Guest House 20 Rooms air- conditioned, furnished and provided with attached bathrooms with dining facilities. Parents or guardians of the students or experts can stay with the approval of the competent authority. Hostel Facilities:: IIIT-NR has four hostels for boys and three for girls. A multi purpose indoor hall with four badminton courts cum a basket ball court, one out door basketball court, two volleyball courts and one football cum cricket ground are available. Indoor game facilities are available in each hostel apart from the SAC (Student Activities Centre).

III. Admission to B.Tech. Programs: Admission to the B.Tech. programmes at IIIT Naya Raipur is governed solely by the JEE (Main) 2026 rank. There are 90 seats available in each CSE, ECE, and DSAI. Additionally there are some female only supernumerary seats and 1 Kashmiri Migrant seat in each branch. Eligible candidates may apply under the following categories: All India Quota Chhattisgarh Quota NTPC Quota

All India Quota: 35% of seats, amounting to 95 seats (32 in CSE, 32 in ECE and 31 in DSAI) are in this category. Additionally there are 24 female only supernumerary seats (8 in each branch), reserved only for female candidates. Candidates who completed their school education in any part of India can apply under this category. These seats will be filled through JoSAA/CSAB 2026 counselling (visit https://josaa.nic.in). So their eligibility will be as per the business rules of JoSAA 2026. All reservations will be as per the Government of India norms. NTPC Quota: 15% of seats, amounting to 40 seats (16 in CSE, 17 in ECE and 17 in DSAI) are in this category. Additionally there are 10 female only supernumerary seats (3 in CSE, 3 in DSAI, 4 in ECE ), reserved only for female candidates. Candidates employed with NTPC or their wards who completed their school education in any part of India can apply under this category. Their

reservations will be as per the Government of India norms. These seats will be filled through the IIIT-NR online counselling process (visit https://www.iiitnr.ac.in/content/b-tech-admission-2026) Candidates seeking admission under NTPC quota seats shall submit a certificate in the prescribed format (Annexure I) from the Nodal Authority of NTPC, certifying that the candidate is eligible to apply for the NTPC quota. The candidates applying for OBC-NCL under All India and NTPC quota must submit the OBC-NCL certificate in the format (Annexure II) provided by the JoSAA 2026. Other formats are not acceptable.

Frequently Asked questions:

1. Placement Participation

Q: Are CMIT M.Tech (DSAI) fellows eligible to participate in campus placement drives along with other M.Tech students? A: Yes, CMIT M.Tech fellows are permitted to participate in campus placement drives as applicable to the other academic programs of IIITNR. However, joining any company is only allowed after successful completion of the M.Tech program. Any deviation from this may invoke the bond clause.

2. Fellowship Eligibility

Q: Can a CMIT M.Tech fellow with a valid GATE score receive the AICTE fellowship of ₹12,500 in addition to the CMIT fellowship? A: No. A student cannot avail of two fellowships simultaneously.

3. Mode of Skill Test

Q: Will the skill test be conducted online or offline? A: The skill test will be conducted in offline mode.

Q: Will the skill test be conducted online or offline? A: The skill test will be conducted in offline mode.

4. Skill Test Syllabus Q: What syllabus or content will the skill test cover? A: Please refer to the official brochure or the program’s webpage for syllabus details.

5. Residential Requirement Q: Is it mandatory for CMIT M.Tech fellows to reside on campus during the program? A: Yes, IIIT Naya Raipur is a fully residential campus. All students are required to stay on campus.

6. Mid-Program Placement Q: What if a CMIT M.Tech fellow receives a placement offer during the course of the program (on-campus or off-campus)? A: Students may only accept such offers after completing the program. Early joining would trigger the bond clause.

7. Post-Program Government Opportunities Q: Are there guaranteed government job opportunities for CMIT M.Tech fellows after program completion? A: There is no provision of any guaranteed Government jobs. However,  it is up to the prevalent norms & rules of Government of Chhattisgarh to consider or not the fellows of the program after the completion of the course.

rules of Government of Chhattisgarh to consider or not the fellows of the program after the completion of the course.

8. Academic Fee Coverage Q: Does the fellowship cover all academic fees such as tuition, registration, examination, and hostel fees? A: The Government of Chhattisgarh sponsors only the tuition fee. Other expenses including hostel accommodation, mess, examination fees, medical insurance, SAC charges, etc., must be borne by the fellows.

9. Accommodation During Government Department Engagement Q: Will accommodation be provided during government department assignments? Will hostel facilities at IIIT-NR be available if the posting is outside campus? A: Fellows will be provided accommodation within the IIIT-NR campus throughout the duration of the program.

10. Equivalence with Regular M.Tech (CSE) Q: Is the CMIT M.Tech program equivalent to the regular M.Tech in CSE? A: Yes, the CMIT M.Tech program is academically equivalent to the regular M.Tech in CSE. Though each and every academic program has its own program structure and curriculum.

Dr. Chandra Shekhar Nishad is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Science, Humanities and Management (SHM). Prior to joining IIIT-NR, he was an Assistant Professor in the Department of Mathematics, School of Technology, Pandit Deendayal Energy University (PDEU) Gandhinagar, India. He has completed M.Sc. (Mathematics & Computing) from IIT Guwahati in 2009 and M.Tech. (Industrial Mathematics & Scientific Computing) from IIT Madras in 2012. He has completed his Ph.D. degree in Applied Mathematics from IIT Kharagpur under the supervision of Prof. G.P Raja Sekhar in 2019. He has received DAAD Scholarship (DAAD IIT Master Sandwich Program) for doing M.Tech. Dissertation at Technical University Darmstadt Germany in 2011. He was the batch topper in M.Tech. (Industrial Mathematics & Scientific Computing) at IIT Madras. He has published more than 20 research papers in journals and conference proceedings of international repute. Currently, he is supervising one Ph.D. student in PDEU Gandhinagar as external co-guide. He has also served as reviewer of papers/articles of many reputed international journals and conferences.

Dr. Darash Adhari is a vocalist, researcher, composer, and academician specializing in Hindustani Classical Music. She earned her Ph.D. from Dayalbagh Educational Institute (DEI), Agra. She previously served as a Guest Faculty in the Department of Music at DEI. Dr. Darash is an accomplished composer with 50 original musical compositions to her credit. Her academic excellence and contributions to Indian music have been recognized through several prestigious honours, including the Sangeet Manishi Raghunath Talegaonkar Award & the International Women Achiever Award. Many students across Agra are receiving vocal training under her guidance and have achieved notable success in prestigious platforms such as the Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi (Lucknow), Yuva Mahotsav, Ninad Sangeet Mahotsav, and Sangeetotsav.

Fellow- IEEE, Fellow- Institution of Engineers, Fellow-The World Academy of Sciences, Fellow-Marconi Society, Fellow-Institution of Electronics and Telecom Engineers, India. Prof. Paulraj is an Emeritus Professor, Department of Electrical Engineering at Stanford University and a Pioneer in MIMO Wireless. He has graduated 50 doctoral and post-doctoral scholars at Stanford. Prof. Paulraj served in the Indian Navy from 1965 to 1991, during which period, he headed the APSOH sonar program, one of India’s most successful military R&D projects. He also founded three national level labs in Artificial Intelligence and Robotics, High Performance Computing and Military Electronics. After joining Stanford in 1991, Paulraj founded Iospan Wireless Inc. (1998) which pioneered MIMO-OFDMA used in 4G, co-founded Beceem Communications Inc. (2004) which became the leader in 4G / WIMAX chip sets and co-founded Rasa Networks (2014) that developed AI tools for WiFi management. Companies & Laboratories founded by Prof. Paulraj:-

1987 CDAC, Bangalore Founding Director

Prof. L.M. Patnaik is currently an Honorary Professor Department of Electronic Systems Engineering (formerly CEDT) at Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bangalore. During March 2008 - August 2011, he was the Vice Chancellor, Defence Institute of Advanced Technology, Deemed University, Pune. He is a Distinguished Lecturer of the IEEE Region 10 and a distinguished Visitor of the IEEE Computer Society for the Asia-Pacific Region. Dr. Mallikharjuna Rao K is currently serving as Assistant Professor (Grade-I) in the Department of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence at the International Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Naya Raipur, Chhattisgarh, India.

Prior to this position, he worked as an Assistant Professor (Senior Grade-I) at VIT-AP University, Andhra Pradesh (2019–2021). He also served as an Associate Professor at Shri Vishnu Engineering College for Women, Bhimavaram (2018–2019). Earlier, he was associated with GITAM University, Visakhapatnam (2011–2018) and Gokaraju Rangaraju Institute of Engineering and Technology, Hyderabad (2007–2011) as an Assistant Professor.

Dr. Rao received his Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering (2018) and M.Tech. in Computer Science (2010) from Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University Hyderabad (JNTUH). He earned his B.Tech. in Information Science and Technology from Acharya Nagarjuna University, Andhra Pradesh, in 2004.

He has successfully secured research funding, including a grant of ₹6 lakhs from the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, for organizing a National Workshop on Data Science Research at GITAM University, and ₹3.69 lakhs from NTPC Ltd. for research activities at IIIT Naya Raipur.

on Data Science Research at GITAM University, and ₹3.69 lakhs from NTPC Ltd. for research activities at IIIT Naya Raipur.

Dr. Rao has published over 60 research papers in reputed international journals and conferences. He holds one Indian granted patent and has two published Indian patents to his credit.

He served as an editorial board member and reviewer for several reputed SCI/WoS/Scopus-indexed journals, including IET Software, IEEE Sensors Journal, CMBBE, IJSAEM, JCS, JSR, IJECE, IJCS, BEEI, and IJSER. He has also chaired technical sessions at major international conferences, including IEEE WIECON-ECE 2022, ICCIDE 2022, and TRIBES 2021. Additionally, he has served as a Technical Program Committee (TPC) member and reviewer for various Springer and IEEE conferences, including WCAIC 2023, ICDSA 2023, CVR 2023, InC4 2023, ICCCT 2023, TENSYMP 2022, AIC 2022, and ICCIS 2022.

Dr. Rao is a Senior Member of IEEE, including IEEE Computational Intelligence Society (CIS) and IEEE Computer Society (CS), and a Life Member of the Computer Society of India (CSI).

His research interests include Artificial Intelligence, particularly Evolutionary Algorithms, Swarm Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Science, Data Mining, Data Privacy, Imbalanced Data Learning, and their applications in healthcare and finance.

Dr. Manoj Kumar Majumder is an Associate Professor in the discipline of Electronics and Communication Engineering at Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee International Institute of Information Technology, Naya Raipur (IIIT-NR), a position he has held since October 2024. Prior to this, he served as an Assistant Professor at the same institute from January 2017 to September 2024. He obtained his Ph.D. from the Microelectronics and VLSI Group, Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering, IIT Roorkee. Dr. Majumder has made significant contributions to research and academia, with over 65 publications in peer-reviewed international journals and more than 56 papers presented at reputed international conferences. He is a co-author of three books: Introduction to Microelectronics to Nanoelectronics: Design and Technology (CRC Press, November 2020), Through Silicon Vias: Materials, Models, Design and Performance (CRC Press, November 2016), and Carbon Nanotube Based VLSI Interconnects: Analysis and Design (Springer, New York, 2014). In addition, he has contributed five book chapters published by CRC Press and Springer. He holds three granted Indian patents. He has successfully completed four sponsored research projects funded by Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF), Govt. of INDIA, Chhattisgarh Council of Science and Technology (CGCOST), and Indian Nanoelectronics User

(ANRF), Govt. of INDIA, Chhattisgarh Council of Science and Technology (CGCOST), and Indian Nanoelectronics User Program INUP (IISc Bangalore), with a total project value of ₹56.15 lakhs. His research interests span Low-Power VLSI Circuits and Systems Design, modeling of VLSI device and circuit performance parameters, emerging electronics, carbon nanotube and graphene nanoribbon-based VLSI interconnects, through-silicon vias, nanomaterials, and their applications. Beyond research and teaching, Dr. Majumder is actively involved in academic and administrative responsibilities at IIIT Naya Raipur. He has served in several key roles, including Controller of Examinations, President of the Students’ Activity Centre, Chairman of the Hostel Management Committee, and Warden. He has delivered technical talks at various national and international conferences and has served as Lead Guest Editor for a special issue titled “Next Generation Low Power VLSI Interconnects and Emerging Technologies” in the journal VLSI Design (Hindawi). Dr. Majumder is an active reviewer for several prestigious journals, including IEEE Transactions on Electromagnetic Compatibility, IEEE Transactions on Nanotechnology, IEEE Electron Device Letters, Microelectronics Journal, IET Micro & Nano Letters, IET Circuits, Devices and Systems, IETE Journal of Research, and other Springer journals. He is also a member of

Systems, IETE Journal of Research, and other Springer journals. He is also a member of several expert committees constituted by government and non-government organizations. In recognition of his academic and research excellence, he has received the “A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Award” and the “Best Research Awards in Engineering, Medicine and Statistics” from the Association of Researchers and Academicians India (ARAI) and VDGOOD Technology Factory in December 2024 and September 2020, respectively. His name has been listed in Marquis Who’s Who in the World. Dr. Majumder is a Senior Member of IEEE and an active member of the IEEE Circuits and Systems Society and the IEEE Electronics Packaging Society.

Dr. Punya P. Paltani is an Assistant Professor of Physics in the Science and Mathematics discipline. Prior to joining IIIT-NR, he was an Assistant Professor in Mody University, Rajasthan. He is a lifetime member of the Indian Physics Association, Optical Society of India, Senior member of Optical Society of America, and Senior IEEE Fellow. He was awarded Best Teacher Award by The Association of Engineers (India), CSIR Fellowship for doctoral research and TUBITAK Fellowship (by TURKISH Govt.) for Post-Doctoral research. Dr. Ruhul Amin is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering Discipline. Prior to joining IIIT Naya Raipur, he was an assistant professor of NIT Jamshedpur. Dr. Amin received doctoral (Ph.D.) degree in Computer Science and Engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology(ISM) Dhanbad, Jharkhand, India, in 2017 and received B.Tech and M.Tech both in Computer Science and Engineering from Maulana Abul Kalam Azad University of Technology, West Bengal, India in 2009 and 2013, respectively. He has authored many technical research papers published in leading international conferences and peer-reviewed international journals from the IEEE, Elsevier, Springer, John Wiley, etc.  He is an Associate Editor of “Security and Privacy” and "Security and communication networks" published by John Wiley and Hindwai respectively. He is an active senior member of IEEE and a member of ACM.

In 2021, Stanford University has released a list that represents the top 2 per cent of the most-cited scientists in various disciplines. In recognition of exceptional research performance demonstrated by production of multiple highly cited papers, Dr. Amin made it to the list of Top 2% of the most cited scientists released by the US-based prestigious standford university.

Dr. Shailesh Khapre is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence at DSPM IIIT-Naya Raipur, C. G. India. He received the B.Tech. Degree (Comp. Sci. & Engg.) from the NIT Rourkela, Orissa, in 2009, and the M.Tech. Degree (Comp. Sci. & Engg.) from Pondicherry University, Puducherry in 2011. He obtained a Ph.D. degree from the Pondicherry University, Puducherry, India in 2019-20 in the area of Information Retrieval. Earlier, he worked with the SRM-IST (Ghaziabad), and Amity University, Noida as an Assistant professor. Dr. Shailesh is a recipient of the Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship (RGNF_2012) for the year 2012-2016 by the UGC, Govt. of India and has published research work in various reputed journals with IEEE, Elsevier, Springer, etc. His current research interest is in Intelligent Information Retrieval, Robot Perceptions, Sensory Fusion, Computer Vision, Machine learning, Localization, Planning, Navigation.

Shrivishal Tripathi is an Associate Professor at the International Institute of Information Technology, Naya Raipur, Chhattisgarh. He previously served as an Assistant Professor at BITS-Pilani, Hyderabad, and NIIT University, Neemrana. He earned his Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from IIT Jodhpur in 2015, an M.E. from PEC University of Technology, Chandigarh, in 2011, and a B.Tech. from Dr. K.N. Modi Institute of Engineering and Technology, Ghaziabad, in 2009. His main research interest includes UWB / MIMO Antenna, Antenna for 5G/6G and IoT, AI in Electromagnetics, ML/DL in RF Circuit Design, Energy Harvesting, UAV, and Signal Modulation/Demodulation Techniques. He has successfully completed 06 sponsored/consultancy projects as PI/Co-PI sanctioned by DST, IGKV Raipur, CCOST, and Mahyco Pvt. Ltd. In addition, 03 more projects are currently in progress. He has published 80+ papers in reputed Journals and international/national conferences. He has organized many workshops and FDP. He serves on the Standing Review Committee for the Radio Altimeter System in DRDO Hyderabad, a Ministry of Defense, Govt. of India division and IIRS-ISRO, Department of Space (DOS) Govt. of India outreach program's coordinator. He contributed in the "National Rogue Drone Policy." under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).

Dr. Srinivasa K G is a Professor of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence Programme at DSPM IIIT-Naya Raipur, C. G. India. Earlier he worked as a Professor at Information Management and Emerging Engineering Department of National Institute of Technical Teachers Training and Research, Chandigarh an autonomous Institute under Ministry of Education, Government of India. He also worked as an Associate Professor at CBP Government Engineering College, New Delhi (through UPSC) between 2016 – 19. He also served as Professor in the Department of CSE at M S Ramaiah Institute of Technology, Bangalore between 2003 – 2016. He received his Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering from Bangalore University in 2007. researcher – He has visited University of Oklahoma, USA, Iowa State University, USA, Hong Kong University, Korean University, National University of Singapore, University of British Columbia, Canada are his few prominent visits. He has authored many books in the area of Learning Analytics, Network Data Analytics, Soft Computing, Social Network Analysis, High Performance Computing, R Programming etc. with prestigious international publishers like Springer, TMH, Oxford, Cengage, and IGI Global. He has edited research monographs in the area of Cyber Physical Systems, Fog Computing and Energy Aware Computing with CRC Press and IGI Global. He has been awarded BOYSCAST Fellowship by DST, Govt. of India, for conducting post-doctoral research work at University of Melbourne, Australia. He is the principal Investigator for many funded projects from AICTE, UGC, DRDO, and DST. He has undertaken consultancy projects worth 60 lakhs towards conducting Professional Development Programmes under World Bank Project. He is the senior member of IEEE and ACM. His recent research areas include Innovative Teaching Practices in Engineering Education, pedagogy; outcomes based education, and teaching philosophy.

Dr. Srishti Bachwani is an Assistant Professor at the International Institute of Information Technology, Naya Raipur (IIIT-NR). She holds a Ph.D. in Marketing from the Indian Institute of Management Lucknow, an MBA in Marketing, and a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science Engineering. Dr. J. Vijaya is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence at DSPM IIIT-Naya Raipur, C. G. India.  She obtained her Ph.D. degree from National Institute of Technology-Tiruchirappalli; India in the area of Data Science. She completed her Bachelor’s degree (Comp. Sci. & Engg.) from MS University-Tirunelveli, India and Masters Degree (Comp. Sci. & Engg.) from Anna University-Tiruchirappalli, India. Her current research interests are Data Analytics, Data Mining, Machine Learning Concepts, Soft computing Techniques, Neural networks and Deep learning, Metaheuristic and swarm Intelligence Algorithms, Evolutionary computation, Fuzzy logic and Rough set theory, Advanced clustering and Big Data Analytics. Totally she has 13 years of teaching experience in various institution and universities. Her objective is to pursue a challenging position in the field of Lecturing where she can effectively develop her skills and contribute them for the development of the Institution. She is a Member of Indian Society of Technical Education (MISTE) and also she acted as a coordinator in various institute level committees. She has published research work in various reputed journals.

DIRECTOR

PROF. (DR.) OM PRAKASH VYAS DIRECTOR, IIIT NAYA RAIPUR

Prof. (Dr.) Om Prakash Vyas is a distinguished academician, researcher, and institutional leader with over three decades of experience in technical education, research, and academic administration. He holds an MJech. in Computer Science from IIT Kharagpur and pursued doctoral research at Technical University of Kaiserslautern, Germany, under a DAAD Fellowship.

As the founding Head of Computer Science at Pt. Ravishankar Shukla University, he established Chhattisgarh's first formal Computer Science programme in 1992. His early initiatives played a pioneering role in extending Computer Science and IT education across a large network of affiliated colleges in Chhattisgarh, helping lay the foundation for the State's subsequent expansion of IT education.
heading_path: Administrative Leadership, Vision, Mission & Contact Hierarchy

text:
a large network of affiliated colleges in Chhattisgarh, helping lay the foundation for the State's subsequent expansion of IT education.

Prof. Vyas has had a long and significant association with IlIT Allahabad, beginning as Assistant Professor during 2002-03, in the formative years of the Institute. He returned to IlIT-A in 2009 as Professor of Information Technology and continued there until 2026, serving in several academic and leadership responsibilities, including as Dean (Research & Development), Dean (Technology Development) and Member of BoG. During this period, he contributed to the Institute’'s academic development, including the conceptualization and introduction of the BTech. programme in IT-Business Informatics in 2019, and coordinated NEP 2020- inspired academic reforms for B.Tech. programs.

He has successfully led several national and international collaborative research projects and has been a sought-after Visiting Professor at multiple global institutions. These include the National Institute of Informatics, Tokyo (Japan, 2010), the University of Paderborn (Germany, 2013-2017), Inria Lille (France, 2015), the University of Messina (Italy, 2016), Norwegian Technical University (Norway), and Bielefeld University (Germany, 2018-2023), where he taught and conducted research every summer for five consecutive years.

Technical University (Norway), and Bielefeld University (Germany, 2018-2023), where he taught and conducted research every summer for five consecutive years.

As Vice Chancellor and Director of IlIT-Naya Raipur, Prof. Vyas has successfully implemented an NEP 2020-inspired BTech. curriculum with a flexible Major-Minor structure, enabling students across engineering branches to pursue interdisciplinary Minors including Business Informatics, Digital Mobility, Digital Humanities, Cyber Security, and Quantum Computing. His leadership emphasizes research excellence, innovation, multidisciplinary education, and industry-academia and international collaboration.

His academic interests span Data Science, Process Intelligence, Business Informatics, Explainable Al, Cyber Security, and Agentic Al. He is currently pursuing international research collaborations in Agentic Al through Indo-Italian initiatives and Cyber Security for Critical Infrastructure through Indo-Norwegian projects.

Annual Report 2022-23 01 The Chancellor Hon'ble Governor of Chhattisgarh, Shri Biswabhusan Harichandan, is the Chancellor of Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee International Institute of Technology - Naya Raipur (IIIT-NR). He assumed the office of the Governor on February 23, 2023. Before serving as the Governor of Chhattisgarh, he was the Governor of the State of Andhra Pradesh. Shri Harichandan is an ardent democrat in all respect who fights for human rights, democracy, democratic values, and citizens’ rights, especially rights of down trodden people and against corruption. He has an enriching political career. He was elected to the Odisha State Legislative Assembly five times. He has served people in various capacities including Revenue Minister, Law Minister, Industry Minister in the then Odisha Government. He also served as Cabinet Minister in 1977 (during emergency), and as the Chairman of the Cabinet Sub- Committee on Rehabilitation and Re-settlement of the displaced persons which was then the best Rehabilitation and Re-settlement Policy of the Country. Shri Harichandan is also a reputed columnist who has written several articles on contemporary political issues, historical, social and cultural matters, which have been published in all leading newspapers of Odisha and some English weeklies of Delhi. He is an inspiring author and has significant literary contributions to his

weeklies of Delhi.
