Annual Report 2022-23 03 Director’s Note It’s indeed a privilege to present the Annual Report 2022-23 of this rapidly growing IIIT-Naya Raipur. About 8 years ago, IIIT-NR embarked upon its journey to realize the State Government’s vision to create a premier technical institute of the country in Chhattisgarh. I am proud to report that “Team IIIT-NR” has successfully converted this dream into reality. With an annual intake of only 80 students in two B. Tech. programmes in 2015, today IIIT-NR offers three B. Tech. programmes, four M. Tech. disciplines, multi- disciplinary M. S. (by Research) and Ph. D. programmes, with a total annual intake of 230 students. These programmes cover a wide range of state-of-the-art technology disciplines. Our industry-oriented teaching-learning pedagogy helped achieve 100% placements in the first four consecutive years, with an average package higher than parallel institutes. Some of our key campus recruiters include Microsoft Research, American Express, Zeiss, Apra Labs, Big Basket, Cognizant, Lumiq, Infosys, KPMG, Capgemini, PharmEasy, Ericsson, Deloitte etc.. In addition, students interested in higher studies secured admissions in renowned academic institutes both in India and abroad. These include IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, University of Massachusetts Amherst (USA), University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (USA), Cornell University (USA), and

Delhi, University of Massachusetts Amherst (USA), University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (USA), Cornell University (USA), and Carnegie Mellon University (USA). Team IIIT-NR firmly believes that both education and research are equally important for a premier Higher Education Institute (HEI). Hence, just like innovative academic programmes, IIIT-NR took a unique approach to carve out its research landscape. It decided to make IIIT-NR “A Living Research Lab for Agriculture, Forestry and Rural Development”, by focusing on applications of ICET (Information, Communication and Electronics Technologies) for agriculture, forestry and rural development. Being situated in Chhattisgarh, a state rich in agriculture and forestry, and dominated by rural population, we chose to focus on these areas so that we can effectively contribute to the inclusive development of the state. I am proud to report that IIIT-NR is currently pursuing several funded research projects in these areas which have resulted in the publication of 242 journal papers, 18 book chapters, 4 books, and 7 patents in the year 2022-23. Our faculty members also conducted several Faculty Development Programs (funded by AICTE) in futuristic technology domains like Robotics, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, etc. ֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍ 3

Annual Report 2022-23 With its firm belief in advancing society through multidisciplinary collaborative research, IIIT- NR has signed MoUs with several premier academic and research institutes. These include All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) Raipur, DRDO, C-DAC, Microsoft Research Lab, Samsung R\&D, Louisiana State University (USA), Wright State University (USA), Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), SECQAI Ltd. (UK) etc. For increased interactions with researchers across the globe, IIIT-NR started its own international conference named TRIBES (Technology, Research, and Innovation for BEtterment of Society). To encourage its members to actively participate in professional societies globally, IIIT-NR has established IEEE Student Branch and IEEE Women in Engineering Affinity Group. In December 2022, it also hosted the IEEE International Women in Engineering Conference. With these initiatives, the institute and the State of Chhattisgarh are gaining increased popularity nationally and internationally as a research hub. Through its entrepreneurship initiatives, IIIT-NR also motivates and nurtures its students to become job creators as an entrepreneur. The institute received the ‘Start Me Up Award’ by Wadhwani Foundation for its entrepreneurship initiatives and active participation in global entrepreneurship competitions. Recognizing the new wave where startups

entrepreneurship initiatives and active participation in global entrepreneurship competitions. Recognizing the new wave where startups will be the dominant job creators of the future, the institute is also setting up an incubation facility in the campus. The institute got 3.5-Star rating by the Institution Innovation Council (IIC), Ministry of Education (MoE) and ‘Peformers Band’ in Atal Rankings of Institutions on Innovation Achievements (ARIIA). To develop the sense of social responsibility in its members, IIIT-NR has established ISR (Institute Social Responsibility) Cell and NSS (National Social Service) unit in its campus. Through these units, IIIT-NR members help less privileged sections of our society in various ways. For example, the institute has adopted two nearby villages (Rakhi and Uparwara) where it conducts special classes for village school children; conducts cleanliness and awareness programmes for the villagers; undertakes projects for tribal and rural development; conducts invited talks for members of other technical institutes to share the best practices of IIIT-NR; conducts summer camps for school children; conducts an annual event called ‘SCIƞTFIC’ (Science and Technology over Fiction) to motivate school children towards career in Science and Technology etc. In addition to our students excelling globally in various ways as mentioned above, several faculty

In addition to our students excelling globally in various ways as mentioned above, several faculty members received international recognitions like selection/ nomination in executive positions in professional societies, elevation to IEEE Senior Member Grade, Gold Faculty Award by Wadhwani Foundation, etc. One of our faculty, Dr. Ruhul Amin, got listed for two consecutive years, among the top 2% most-cited scientists globally in the list released by Stanford University, USA. To sum up, 2022-23 has been a year of success and accelerated growth of IIIT-NR. I acknowledge that the success and the brand that IIIT-NR has earned in this short span would not have been possible without the wholehearted support of Govt. of Chhattisgarh and NTPC and our visionary Board members for their guidance and support in all matters. I extend my sincere thanks to all stakeholders including the brilliant efforts of talented students, academic accomplishments of our faculty members and committed staff. Annual Report 2022-23 04 About the Institute Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee International Institute of Information Technology – Naya Raipur (IIIT-NR) is a joint venture by Govt. of Chhattisgarh and National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC). The institute is established by the International Institute of Information Technology University Act, 2013 of the Govt. of Chhattisgarh “to promote and facilitate studies, research, incubation and extension work in Information Technology and in its application domain and related areas of knowledge and to achieve excellence in these fields and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.” As enshrined in the Act, IIIT-Naya Raipur is committed to pursue excellence in higher education, research and development in Information Technology (IT) and associated disciplines. It firmly believes in bestowing knowledge dissemination and imparting entrepreneurial skills to the students to enable them to address real world problems. To empower this vision, IIIT-NR fosters state-of-the-art research and product development laboratories to carry out inter-disciplinary research and product development endeavours. The institute is mentored by a highly eminent board comprising of industry leaders, erudite academicians and administrators. ֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍ 5

Annual Report 2022-23 IIIT-NR Campus and Location IIIT-NR's fifty-acre fully residential campus is located in the smart city of Nava Raipur, Atal Nagar approximately 23 Kms from Raipur - the capital city of Chhattisgarh state. Raipur is one of the unique cities where various Institutions of National Importance (INIs) and premier academic institutions like IIT, IIM, AIIMS, NIT, HNLU, PRSU, IGKV and IIIT-NR are located in close proximity. Availability of these premier higher educational and research organisations at one place makes the city a perfect educational hub. It gives students and scholars a perfect platform with plenty of opportunities and appropriate ambience and ecosystem for teaching, learning and research on wide spectrum of subjects. The city is well connected by air, rail and road to all parts of the country. The vibrant lush green campus of IIIT- NR is enabled with Wi-Fi connectivity, CCTV surveillance, hi-tech security measures and excellent amenities for sports and recreation. The modern architecture of the buildings and the campus's serene environment fosters an ambiance for creativity and innovation. The classrooms and labs are equipped with state-of-the-art technologies for teaching, learning and research. IIIT-NR Campus 6 ֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍

Annual Report 2022-23 Labs @ IIIT-NR To provide students with hands-on experience for strong practical and technical skills with focus on real world problems and also to facilitate quality teaching, learning, and research, the IIIT- NR has setup various state-of-the-art labs. These are as follows:-  The 3D Printing & Fabrication Lab The 3D Printing and Fabrication Lab is a state-of-the-art digital manufacturing space. It allows students to quickly fabricate parts from computer generated designs to rapidly iterate prototype designs.  VLSI Embedded System Lab VLSI Embedded System Lab is well equipped with industry standard VLSI tools and hardware resources like Raspberry PI board, Universal FPGA/CPLD Card, XILINX FPGA -ADD ON Card, XILINX FPGA ZYNQ, etc. The primary objective of the lab is to provide hands-on experience to students in the field of analog, digital and mixed-signal circuit design so that they can conduct world class research, produce competitive results, create solutions tailored to society's needs, and to disseminate knowledge for public use.  BigData Computing Lab BigData Computing Lab enables training and research in all aspects of large and distributed information systems (e.g. system development, testing, maintenance, data integration, networking, and application development). It prepares students for emerging cutting-edge technologies in the fast-growing

integration, networking, and application development). It prepares students for emerging cutting-edge technologies in the fast-growing IT industry such as BigData Computing, Healthcare Informatics, Data Integration and Data Analytics.  Internet of Things & Sensors Lab IoT Lab is at the forefront of developing both hardware, including novel sensors, communication platform and analytics for Internet of Things (IoT) and smart environments. The IoT lab provides necessary software and equipment to develop and characterize novel smart sensors for IoT applications. Along with these, the lab is equipped with various kits like Smart Healthcare, Smart Agriculture, Smart Village/ City.  Network Lab Fully equipped with Dell PCs and Netsim, Ns2 Simulators, the Network lab enables students to conduct research in the area of wired and wireless networks. The lab also emphasizes experimental research in the area of communication networking.  Artificial Intelligence & Deep Learning (AIDL) Lab The AIDL Lab enables the students to carry out experiments and research on a variety of topics within Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning with focus on using real world problems to discover computationally hard problems of modelling uncertainty, learning predictive models and enabling decision making. ֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍ 25

Annual Report 2022-23  Communication Lab The Communication Lab provides necessary hardware and software resources to the undergraduate and research students of Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE) for enhancing their skills in the communication field. Theory in the classroom is translated directly into practice with the help of the Ettus USRP software defined radio platform and Matlab/National Instruments LabVIEW. The emphasis is on physical layer concepts rather than implementation considerations.  Electronic Circuit Lab The primary objective of this Lab is to provide engineering skills by way of breadboard circuit design with electronic devices and components and to analyse various electronic circuits and digital circuits such as multi-vibrators, Flip-Flop circuits, applications of operational amplifiers, RC coupled amplifiers, oscillators, etc. so that students are able to understand the practical aspects of basic electronics theory. It also enables the students to simulate and test the Analog, Digital and mixed electronics circuits using Verilog, Matlab and OrCAD software.  Computer Programming Lab Computer Programming Lab is a hands-on project and assignment-based learning space where students can gain strong practical and technical skills in various programming languages, including C, Python, Java, UNIX/Linux: shell, tools, utilities and programming

skills in various programming languages, including C, Python, Java, UNIX/Linux: shell, tools, utilities and programming environments, user interfaces, and software engineering principles.  Antenna & Microwave Circuit Design Lab This Lab supports intermediate and advanced courses in Electromagnetics and Microwave Engineering. The microwave laboratories provide the necessary support for training the students in the area of RF and Microwave Engineering. It offers analysis and simulation of various components and devices to understand the basics of RF and microwave engineering, to boost the quality of engineering education, deepen understanding, and provide the necessary practical skills to young minds.  Data Science Lab Data Science Lab is configured to not only facilitate students to practice basic programming in C, C++ and JAVA; but also to learn advanced technologies of computer science such as Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning and Data Mining. The Lab facilitates database designing and management through dedicated tools such as Oracle and MySQL, and related computing paradigm and frameworks.  Language Lab The blended methodology used at the Language Laboratory caters to the language needs of students by providing them suitable environment for self-paced effective language learning. Annual Report 2022-23 Training and Placement The Institute has a dedicated Training and Career Cell (TCC) which endeavours to provide good career opportunities to students. TCC is headed by Dr. Amit Agrawal, Assistant Professor (Management) and mentored by Dr. Pradeep K. Sinha, Director, IIIT-NR. TCC keeps close contact with potential employers for organising campus placements and internships drives for students. It also maintains lively relationships with industry partners through industry–academia interactions. Steps to Improve Placement With rapid technological advancement in industry, the present-day campus placement of students has become more challenging and competitive. The Training and Career Cell (TCC) undertakes several initiatives to prepare students to successfully overcome these challenges and grab their desired career opportunities. Towards this, to make students employable and industry ready, the TCC facilitates an effective industry–institute interaction and organises various activities and programmes in coordination with Students Activity Centre (SAC) of the Institute. Some of these skill-set enhancing and career oriented programmes are:-  Training programmes on latest skills-sets required in industry s e r u  Skill-enhancing and industry oriented competitions s a e

Annual Report 2022-23 1 0 Patents and Publications With the changing technological landscape and society needs, research has become increasingly important. Through research, educational institutions can make significant contributions to the society as well as the economy of the country. Further, quality of research are considered hallmark of quality of teaching, learning and research of any educational Institution. Considering the significance of research, IIIT-NR has been actively involved in quality research since its inception. As a result, the Institute has been making consistent progress in the field of research publications and patents. Since its inception in 2015 till 2022-23, the Institute got awarded 23 patents and over 200 scholarly publications (research papers, books etc.) which is the testimony to the quality of research being done at IIIT-NR. In addition, there is consistent increase in funded initiatives. In the year 2018-19, the funded initiative was of Rs. 50 Lakh which has increased by manifold over the years. In the year 2022-23, the Institute got awarded 7 patents, published 84 scholarly publications and had funded initiatives of over Rs. 370 Lakh. Annual Report 2022-23  A book co-authored by Prof. Srinivasa K. G., titled ‘Learning, Teaching, and Assessment Methods for Contemporary Learners: Pedagogy for the Digital Generation’, was published by Springer Nature. The textbook tackles the matter of contemporary learners’ needs, and introduces modern learning, teaching, and assessment methods. It provides a deeper understanding of these methods so that the students and teachers can create teaching and learning opportunities for themselves and others. This textbook showcases various modern learning, teaching, and assessment methods for contemporary learners in an increasingly digital environment. Development of Software to Filter Toxic Comments on Social Media In order to keep the user safe on social media and to maintain positivity on social media, a group of three students namely Sayantan Roy, Rishi Shounak, and Vivek Kumar, under the guidance of Dr. Vivek Tiwari, worked on the development of a ‘Software that Filters Toxic Comments on Social Media’. This software works on all social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, and YouTube. The software works on a machine learning model. Expert Talks  An expert talk on ‘Development of Compressed CNN Models for Plant Disease Identification’ was delivered on October 19, 2022 by Prof. K. K. Biswas, retired Professor, IIT-Delhi. The talk was related to the work done in the area of Automatic Plant Disease Identification from leaf images, such as tomato, grapes, and cucumber. A lot of literature is available on
section_title: Section and IEEE Madhya Pradesh Section
heading_path: Section and IEEE Madhya Pradesh Section

text: leaf images, such as tomato, grapes, and cucumber. A lot of literature is available on applications of deep learning to solve this issue. However, the sizes of the CNN (Convolution Neural Networks) is so huge that it requires specialized professional equipment. His work relates to reducing the size of these networks, so that they can be easily deployed on small devices like Raspberry Pi or mobile phones. Using heuristic algorithms like differential evolution and Particle Swarm Optimization, the huge CNN models have been compressed to more than 80% of their size, while maintaining the accuracy of disease identification. 60 ֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍

text: Annual Report 2022-23 Take da Bait : Take da Bait is a debate club at IIIT-Naya Raipur. The club's purpose is to provide a platform for students to discuss and debate current trends and issues in the world, and to help members form their own opinions on these topics. The club is intended to help students connect to the changing socio-political environment of the world and to understand the potential advantages and disadvantages of technology and its impact on the world. The club believes that by discussing and debating important issues, members will be better equipped to be informed citizens and future leaders. Annual Report 2022-23 Group Discussion on India’s Journey from Partition to Present The Model United Nations club of IIIT-NR conducted a group discussion on ‘What If - India’s Journey from Partition to Present’ on September 09, 2022. The objective of the event was to provide a platform to students to share their opinions on some of the most important events that have defined India’s journey since independence. This event proved to be helpful in encouraging students to learn about the major political, social and economic events of our post-independence history. A platform for group discussion also helped students to develop leadership and public speaking skills. Model United Nations (MUN) Conference The Model United Nations (MUN) Club of IIIT-NR conducted a 2-day conference under the two committees namely- All India Political Parties Meet (AIPPM) and Disarmament and International Security Committee (DISEC). The AIPPM discussed on the topic ‘Safeguarding the Integrity of the Democracy in Recent Times’, by discussing developments, including the persecution of journalists and independent media and analyzing the significance and aptness of the laws like UAPA, NRC and CAA. On the other hand, DISEC focused on the ‘Illicit Trade of Small Arms and Light Weapons’ and the ‘Weaponization of Big Data’. The motive of the event was to instigate interest among the students in world politics

The motive of the event was to instigate interest among the students in world politics as well as in various political and civic affairs of our democracy. The event was very useful for students to develop leadership and public speaking skills. Chai Pe Charcha Model United Nations (MUN) club of IIIT-NR organized a group discussion ‘Chai Pe Charcha’, on January 19, 2023. The topic of discussion was ‘The State of Media in Contemporary Indian Democracy and Social Media's Relevance and Role in Shaping Our Country's Future Politics’. The participants discussed various aspects like the independence of media, the neutrality of facts, the role of media and social media in contemporary policy, the relevance of social media trends, and media reforms, among others. Overall, it was a healthy, engaging, and insightful discussion that enhanced the understanding of the current political and geopolitical scenario of the participants. 74 ֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍

Classes by IIIT-NR for Underprivileged Children As a part of the ‘Rural Transformation Through Education Initiative’ of National Service Scheme (NSS), the NSS unit of IIIT-NR, in collaboration with the Institute Social Responsibility (ISR) cell conducts weekly classes in the local schools of Uparwara and Nawagaon villages. The initiative focuses on the overall personality development of underprivileged students through education, awareness and physical fitness. The volunteers of various subjects like Mathematics, Basic Sciences, Humanities etc. take turns visiting the schools every Saturday and Sunday. They also organize multiple games for the students and spread awareness about the importance of games and sports for their physical well-being and overall personality development. The drive is a part of various initiatives taken by NSS, IIIT-Naya Raipur, under the ‘Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav’ celebrations. 80 ֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍

Annual Report 2022-23 Education through Social Work IIIT-NR conducts various programs as part of its social responsibility for the development of children of nearby villages. As part of this, the ISR team of IIIT- NR distributed stationery items and chocolates to the children of the Government Primary School, Nawagaon, Nava Raipur. The team members also motivated the children for planting trees and educated them about the importance of plants and how they should save trees for the benefit of mankind. Mr. R K Sinha, Head Master of the school, thanked IIIT-NR team. Panchayat President, Mr. Sujeet Ghidoude, also expressed his gratitude to the IIIT-NR for such initiatives. Awareness Camp on Poshan Abhiyan Under the aegis of Poshan Abhiyan of the Government of India, the National Service Scheme (NSS) unit of IIIT-NR, in collaboration with Institute Social Responsibility (ISR) cell, organized an awareness drive in the nearby Government School of Nawagaon, Naya Raipur. The campaign aimed to disseminate knowledge about the importance of nutrition in our lives and to promote practices that nurture health, wealth, and immunity to disease and malnutrition. The Poshan Abhiyan is a Government of India’s flagship program to improve the nutritional outcome for children, adolescent girls, pregnant women, and lactating mothers. The school administration appreciated the efforts and

children, adolescent girls, pregnant women, and lactating mothers. The school administration appreciated the efforts and contributions of the NSS unit of IIIT-NR towards various schemes such as the Swachchha Bharat Abhiyaan, Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav, Poshan Abhiyan, and so on, thereby invoking a sense of responsibility and social service among the volunteers. Annual Cultural Programme at Learning Centre The Institute Social Responsibility (ISR) cell of IIIT-NR organized the Annual Cultural Programme by nearby village school children studying in the Learning Centre run by IIIT-NR, on the occasion of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose’s Birthday, on January 23, 2023. The Learning Center at Uparwara, Naya Raipur, named as ‘Vidyasagar - Phule Learning Center’ has been continuing since 2021. Students, research scholars, and faculties of IIIT-NR teach at this Learning Center every Saturday and Sunday with the aim of imparting better scientific education to village school students. The programme was attended by faculty, staff, students of IIIT-NR and the villagers. ֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍ 81

Annual Report 2022-23 BMC Walkathon IIIT-NR students participated in a walkathon organized by Balco Medical Centre, Nava Raipur on the occasion of its foundation day on March 23, 2023. The event aimed to raise awareness about cancer. It began with a presentation about the disease and its prevalence in society. The speakers highlighted the importance of early detection and prevention measures to fight against cancer. They also shared some of the current research and progress being made in the field of cancer treatment. The presentation was followed by the walkathon. World Consumer Rights Day 2023 The Student Activity Center (SAC) and National Service Scheme (NSS) of IIIT-Naya Raipur in association with the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Raipur, as part of BIS’s ‘Quality Connect Campaign 3.0’ conducted a door-to-door survey at its campus at Nava Raipur from March 15 – 19, 2023, to spread awareness about the importance of standardization. BIS is the National Standards Body of India, established under the BIS Act 2016 for the harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. 82 ֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍

In compliance with the decisions of Hon’ble Supreme Court of India and consequent Gazette notification of “University Grant Commission Regulations 2013” for curbing the Menace of Ragging in Higher Educational Institutions and also as notified by AICTE vide its notification no. 37-3/Legal/AICTE/2009 dated 25-03-2009, the competent authority has constituted following Committees as part of Anti ragging measures in IIITNR campus;

- VC & Director - Chair - Dean (Academics) - Member - Chairman (HMC)- Member - SAC President - Member - Dr. Sresha Yadav nee Ghosh - Member - Representative of parents (fresher, Senior) - Student representatives (fresher, Senior) - Registrar - Member Secretary

The proposed Anti-Ragging Squads shall be empowered to inspect all such places which are vulnerable to incidents of ragging and shall ensure vigil in all such locations. Hostel Level Squad shall also be empowered to inspect all places in the Hostel which are vulnerable to incidents of ragging and shall ensure vigil in all such locations. Interpretation 1) The regulations contained in Table ‘H’ of Schedule I of the Companies Act, 2013 shall apply to this Company. In addition, following articles shall apply in so far as they are not inconsistent with Table ‘H’. 2) In the interpretation of these articles, unless repugnant to the subject or context: a) “The Act” means the Companies Act, 2013 or any statutory modifications or re- enactment thereof for the time being in force. b) “Annual General Meeting” means a general meeting of the members held in accordance with the provisions of Section 96 of the Act. c) “Auditors” means and includes those persons appointed as such by the Company from time to time. d) “Board” or “Board of Directors” means the Board of Directors of the Company. e) “Company” “The Company” or “This Company” means the IIIT-NR FOUNDATION FOR

f) “Director’s” means the Directors for time being of the Company, or as the case may be, the directors assembled at a Board. g) “Extra-ordinary General Meeting” means an extra-ordinary general meeting of the members duly called and constituted and any adjourned holding thereof. h) “Member” means a person who agrees in writing to become a member of the company and whose name is entered in the register of members of the company. i) “Meeting” or “General Meeting” means a meeting of members.

j) “Month” means a calendar month. k) “Office” means the Registered Office for the time being of the Company. l) “Person/s” includes, partnership, company, and association of persons. m) A “Resolution” shall be an “Ordinary Resolution” when at a General Meeting of which the notice required under the Act has been duly given, the Votes cast (whether on a show of hands, or on a poll, as the case may (be) in favour of the resolution (including the casting vote, if any of the Chairperson) by the members, who being entitled so to do, vote in person, or where proxies are allowed, by proxy exceed the votes, if any, cast against the resolution by members so entitled and voting. n) “Seal” means the Common Seal for the time being of the Company. o) “Special Resolution” shall have the meaning assigned thereto by Section 189 of the Act. p) “Written” and “In Writing” including printing, lithography and other modes of representing or reproducing words in a visible form. q) Words importing the singular number include, where the context admits or requires, the plural and vice-versa. r) Words importing the masculine gender also include the feminine gender. s) “These presents” or “Regulations” shall means these Articles of Association as originally framed or altered from time to time and shall include the Memorandum where context so requires. t) “Section” or “Sec” means a Section of The

the Memorandum where context so requires. t) “Section” or “Sec” means a Section of The Companies Act,2013. u) “Appellate Tribunal” means the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal constitute under Section 410 of The Companies Act2013. 3) Unless the context otherwise requires, words or expressions contained in these regulations shall have the same meaning as in the Act or any statutory modification thereof in force at the date at which these regulations become binding on the company. 4) The company shall be a “PRIVATE COMPANY” –and accordingly a) Number of members shall be two excluding i) persons who are in the employment of the company and ii) persons who, having been formerly in the employment of the company, were members and have continued to be members after the employment ceased, shall not be included in the number of members; b) Prohibits any invitation to the public to subscribe for any securities of the company.

a) The number of members with which the company proposes to be registered is two, but the board of directors may, from time to time, whenever the company or business of the company requires it, register an increase of members. Such increase shall be made through clause amendment of this clause. b) The subscribers to the Memorandum and such other persons as the Board shall admit to membership will be members of the company.

A member of the Company shall cease to be one on, the happening of any of the following events: a) on his becoming bankrupt or if he is found to be of unsound mind or on he is convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude; b) on his / its voluntary resignation; c) on dissolution of the Member Company; d) if on the recommendation of the Board of Directors, after giving the member an opportunity to explain at a general meeting of the Company, a majority of three fourths of the members present thereat, decide that a member has been acting in derogation of the Company.

Subject to the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 a separate register of members shall be maintained in which shall be entered the name and address and such other information about each member as the Board of Directors may from time to time decide.

a) The administration of the affairs of the Company shall be vested with the Board of Directors. b) Unless otherwise determined by the Company in the General meeting the number of Directors of the Company shall not be more than fifteen and not less than two. c) The following persons shall be appointed as Directors of the Company, by virtue of their office in Shyama Prasad Mukherjee International Institute of Information Technology, Naya Raipur (IIIT-NR).

Remuneration if any shall be paid to the directors subject to clause V of the memorandum of association. i) In addition to the remuneration payable to them in pursuance of the Act, the directors may be paid all travelling, hotel and other expenses properly incurred by them. j) In attending the returning from meetings of the Board of Directors or any committee thereof or general meetings of the Company; or k) In connection with the business of the company.

a) The Board of Directors may meet for the dispatch of business, adjourn and otherwise regulate its meetings, as it thinks fit. b) The Chairperson, and in his absence a director shall, at any time, summon a meeting of the Board. c) Save as otherwise expressly provided in the Act, questions arising at any meeting of the Board shall be decided by a majority of votes. d) In case of equality of votes, the chairperson shall have a second or casting vote. e) The continuing directors may act notwithstanding any vacancy in the Board but, if and so

text: d) No business shall be transacted at any general meeting unless a quorum of members is present at the time when the meeting proceeds to business. e) The quorum requirement for Board meetings shall be either 8 members or 25% of total strength whichever is less. In any other case, the meeting shall stand adjourned to the same day in the next week, at the same time and place, or to such other day and at such other time and place as the Board may determine. g) If at the adjourned meeting a quorum is not present within half an hour from the time appointed for the meeting, the members present shall be a quorum. h) The chairperson may, if any, of the Board shall preside as chairperson at every general meeting of the company. i) The chairperson may, with the consent of any meeting at which a quorum is present, and shall if so directed by the meeting, adjourn the meeting from time to time and from place to place. j) No business shall be transacted at any adjourned meeting other than the business left unfinished at the meeting from which the adjournment took place. k) In the case of an equality of votes, whether

A Professor Dhananjai Pandey is an internationally renowned educator and researcher in the field of Materials Science and Technology. His professional career started in 1977 as a Faculty Member in BHU/IIT (BHU) and he retired as Professor (HAG) in 2017 but continued as Institute Professor for another five years. He is presently a Distinguished Professor of BHU (for life) and IIT Bhilai. A widely travelled scientist, Prof. Pandey has delivered Invited talks/Keynote addresses/ Plenary lectures at very large number of International and National Conferences held within India and abroad. He has published over 200 research articles in journals of international repute, books and book-series with over 8000 citations (14 papers with over 100 citations) and an h-index of 49. He also holds several patents to his credit. He is a Fellow of all the three premier science academies of India (Indian National Science Academy, Indian Academy of Sciences, National Academy of Sciences of India) and a Fellow of the Asia Pacific Academy of Materials. He is a recipient of several awards/medals (INSA Young Scientist Medal, Materials Research Society of India Medal, MRSI Annual Prize and MRSI Distinguished Lectureship award, Homi Bhabha Fellowship Award, DAE Raja Ramanna Award, Pt Jubilee Award of Indian Science Congress, J C Bose National Fellowship award etc). He has He was Coordinator (Head) of the

J C Bose National Fellowship award etc). He has He was Coordinator (Head) of the School of Materials Science and Technology at IT,BHU, first Director in the transition phase and Dean (Faculty Affairs) of IIT BHU. Under his leadership, the School of Mater Sci & Tech emerged as an Internationally reputed Centre of research and teaching in advanced functional materials. As a Dean of Faculty Affairs, policy documents for Salary fixation, Faculty Recruitment and Promotion of deserving existing faculty members as per IIT norms were developed and successfully implemented.

Professor Pandey has been Member of various committees of DST, CSIR, DRDO, UGC, INSA, IASc as well as Member of Governing Body/Council and Executive Council of IIT (BHU), BHU and SU, IUAC etc. Professor Pandey has been Vice President and President of the Indian Crystallographic Association and Vice President of the Materials Research Society of India and is currently President of the Neutron Scattering Society of India. Professor Pandey has served as Co-editor of the leading International journals published by the International Union of Crystallography, Acta Crystallographica Section A and Journal of Applied Crystallography (first Indian), and Member of Editorial Boards of International journals (Phase Transitions, Materials Science Forum and Zeitscrift-fur-kristallographie) as well as Indian journals (Bulletin of Materials Science and Praman-a Physics Journal). He presently serves on the editorial advisory boards of Zeitscrift-fur-kristallographie and Bulletin of Materials Science. He has served on many important international bodies like Ewald Prize Committee (the highest award in crystallography) and Asia-Oceania Neutron Scattering Association (AONSA) Prize Committee, Commission on Aperiodic Crystals, Commission on Inorganic Materials and Minerals, Commission on Mathematical and Theoretical Crystallography (MaThCryst), Sub-Committee on Nomenclature for Phase Transitions of

Minerals, Commission on Mathematical and Theoretical Crystallography (MaThCryst), Sub-Committee on Nomenclature for Phase Transitions of the International Union of Crystallography (IUCr). He also served as Chairman of the MaThCryst Commission of the IUCr, being only the third Indian to be elected as Chairman of any one of the IUCr Commissions over the last seven decades. He is a founding Member of EC of AONSA and continues to be its Member from India at present.

Prof. Rajiv Prakash is the Director of IIT Bhilai. He was appointed to this position by the Hon’ble President of India in her capacity as the Visitor of IIT Bhilai. A Professor of Materials Science and Technology at IIT (BHU) Varanasi, Prof. Prakash has held several key academic and administrative responsibilities, including Head of the School of Materials Science and Technology (twice), Dean (R&D), founder coordinator of the Central Instrument Facility, and IPR Cell of the Institute. He has made major translational contributions in sensor and biosensor engineering by integrating conducting polymers, nanomaterials, smartphone-based diagnostics, IoT-enabled sensing, and automated analysis. His technologies include field-deployable systems for arsenic detection in water, PSA-based cancer diagnostics, glucose sensing, and point-of-care platforms for kidney-related biomarkers and sickle-cell anaemia. Several of these technologies have reached advanced readiness levels and have been transferred to industry. His broader engineering contributions also include polymer composites for optical storage and railway applications, corrosion protection using conducting polymers and green inhibitors, charge-storage materials, and materials for green-energy applications. Prof. Prakash has published more than 270 refereed journal papers (Google Scholar h-index of 53), holds 25 patents (with 3

than 270 refereed journal papers (Google Scholar h-index of 53), holds 25 patents (with 3 technology transfer). His recognitions include the Young Scientist Award, INAE Young Engineer Award, MRSI Medal, election as Academician of the Asia Pacific Academy of Materials, and the Lifetime Engineering Excellence Award 2025 from The Institution of Engineers (India), Bhilai. As Director of IIT Bhilai and Chairman of IIT Bhilai Innovation and Technology Foundation (IBITF), a DST NM-ICPS Technology Innovation Hub, he has advanced innovation-led institutional growth. His recent leadership contributions include AI-enabled Vidya Samiksha Kendra initiatives for data-driven school governance in Chhattisgarh, the proposed IT Park in Durg, and the Tribal Research and Innovation Park (TRIP) in Bastar, which seeks to integrate deep-tech solutions with traditional knowledge for sustainable livelihood and regional development.

Shri Neeraj Jalota is a senior power sector professional with over 37 years of distinguished experience encompassing project development, operations, maintenance, and coal mining. He holds an M.Tech in Industrial Engineering from IIT Delhi and a Post Graduate Diploma in Business Management from MDI Gurgaon, reflecting a strong blend of technical depth and managerial leadership. Currently, Shri Jalota serves as the Executive Director, Unified Shared Services Centre (USSC), an integrated single-window platform responsible for materials procurement and contract management for NTPC stations nationwide. In this role, he has played a pivotal part in driving process standardization, operational efficiency, and enterprise-wide integration of shared services. In addition, he holds the responsibility of Regional Executive Director (WR-II), as the administrative head of five major thermal power stations located at Korba, Sipat, and Lara in Chhattisgarh, and Gadarwara and Khargone in Madhya Pradesh. His mandate encompasses oversight of Operations and Maintenance activities for an aggregate operating capacity of 10,100 MW, as well as strategic supervision of ongoing capacity expansion projects totaling 4,000 MW, including 1,600 MW each at Lara and Gadarwara, and 800 MW at Sipat.

He has rendered his remarkable finesse in the Operation & Maintenance of various power projects spread across all parts of India. Before coming to Lara he was Head of Project of NTPC - Koldam. Shri Subhash Thakur is firmly committed to his responsibility towards constantly striving to set new benchmarks of efficiency and Operation Management of the power stations. With benevolence at heart, Shri Subhash Thakur is philanthropic and is actively involved in various social welfare activities as well.

Ms. Premlata is a seasoned HR leader with over 35 years of distinguished experience in the Indian power sector, encompassing Thermal, Hydro, Gas, Joint Ventures and taken-over power projects across India. Having joined NTPC as an Executive Trainee, she has held a wide range of leadership positions throughout her career and brings deep expertise across the entire spectrum of Human Resource Management. She currently serves as the Executive Director (Strategic HRD & Talent Development) & Head NTPC-PMI, where she leads the organisation's enterprise-wide agenda on competency development, learning and development, leadership nurturing, and capability building. In this capacity, she is spearheading initiatives aimed at developing a future-ready, agile, and high-performing workforce aligned with NTPC's strategic priorities and its transition towards a sustainable energy future.

Prof. (Dr.) Om Prakash Vyas is a distinguished academician, researcher, and institutional leader with over three decades of experience in technical education, research, and academic administration. He holds an M.Tech. in Computer Science from IIT Kharagpur and pursued doctoral research at Technical University of Kaiserslautern, Germany, under a DAAD Fellowship. As the founding Head of Computer Science at Pt. Ravishankar Shukla University, he established Chhattisgarh’s first formal Computer Science programme in 1992. His early initiatives played a pioneering role in extending Computer Science and IT education across a large network of affiliated colleges in Chhattisgarh, helping lay the foundation for the State’s subsequent expansion of IT education. Prof. Vyas has had a long and significant association with IIIT Allahabad, beginning as Assistant Professor during 2002–03, in the formative years of the Institute. He returned to IIIT-A in 2009 as Professor of Information Technology and continued there until 2026, serving in several academic and leadership responsibilities, including as Dean (Research & Development), Dean (Technology Development) and Member of BoG. During this period, he contributed to the Institute’s academic development, including the conceptualization and introduction of the B.Tech. programme in IT–Business Informatics in 2019, and coordinated NEP 2020-inspired

text: and introduction of the B.Tech. programme in IT–Business Informatics in 2019, and coordinated NEP 2020-inspired academic reforms for B.Tech. programs. He has successfully led several national and international collaborative research projects and has been a sought-after Visiting Professor at multiple global institutions. These include the National Institute of Informatics, Tokyo (Japan, 2010), the University of Paderborn (Germany, 2013–2017), Inria Lille (France, 2015), the University of Messina (Italy, 2016), Norwegian Technical University (Norway), and Bielefeld University (Germany, 2018–2023), where he taught and conducted research every summer for five consecutive years. As Vice Chancellor and Director of IIIT-Naya Raipur, Prof. Vyas has successfully implemented an NEP 2020-inspired B.Tech. curriculum with a flexible Major–Minor structure, enabling students across engineering branches to pursue interdisciplinary Minors including Business Informatics, Digital Mobility, Digital Humanities, Cyber Security, and Quantum Computing. His leadership emphasizes research excellence, innovation, multidisciplinary education, and industry–academia and international collaboration. His academic interests span Data Science, Process Intelligence, Business Informatics, Explainable AI, Cyber Security, and Agentic AI. He is currently pursuing international research collaborations in Agentic AI

The Institute in itself is a State University established by the Government of Chhattisgarh and recognized by UGC.

heading_path: To which university and technical board the Institute is affiliated?

text: The first academic session of the institute commenced from Aug 2015 in its own campus.

The Institute currently offers the following programs:-

a) 4 Years B.Tech. in (ECE)

b)4 Years B.Tech. in (CSE)

c)4 Years B.Tech. in (DSAI)

d)2 Years M.Tech. in (CSE)

e)2 Years M.Tech. in (ECE)

f) Ph.D. in (ECE)

g) Ph.D. in (CSE)

h) Ph.D. in (Physics)

i) Ph.D. in (Mathematics)

j) Ph.D. in (English)

k) Ph.D. in (Management)
The admission to B.Tech programs begins in May-June.
section_title: When does admission for B.Tech programs begin?
heading_path: When does admission for B.Tech programs begin?

text: Admission to the undergraduate program of the DSPM IIIT-NR is based strictly on the merit of the candidate as inferred from their performance in JEE (Joint Entrance Examination). The minimum eligibility for applying for the B.Tech program under Chhattisgarh quota at IIIT-NR is 50% aggregate marks in Physics and Mathematics (45% for SC/ST/OBC/PWD candidates) in their 12th standard examination. The eligibility for applying for the B.Tech program under All India category and NTPC quota is as per JoSAA guidelines.

text: Ragging of any kind is strictly prohibited in the Institution. For admission to its programs under CG Quota , the institute follows the Chhattisgarh State Government policy on reservation of 30% to Women. However , for admission under All India Quota & NTPC , Government of India policy on reservation applies.

Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Next Generation Networks Objective: To promote research and innovation in this highly promising area, IIIT Nava Raipur has setup a 5G testbed in its CoE. The CoE has been established in line with Govt. of India’s goal to build indigenous testbeds that closely resemble real-world 5G deployments. Lab Facilities & Equipment: This 5G waveform generation and analysis reference solution combine hardware, software and measurement expertise providing the essential components of a flexible 5G waveform generation and analysis test platform. The reference solution enables engineers and researchers to generate and analyze a variety of 3GPP 5G NR waveforms at RF, centimeter-wave, and millimeter-wave frequencies with modulation bandwidths of up to 2 GHz, with an emphasis on 5G 3GPP NR activity in the 28 GHz and 37 - 39 GHz bands. 5G testbed includes Signal Analyzer (2 Hz to 50 GHz), Vector signal generator (250 kHz to 44 GHz), Arbitrary Waveform Generator (14 Bit / 8GSa/s and 12 Bit / 12 GSa/s), Oscilloscope (1 GHz 4 channel) and other basic facilities. IIIT- NR has also developed the anechoic chamber for characterization, configurable software like SystemVue, MATLAB, and Labview. It also has Multi GPU SMP Server to incorporate machine learning applications in communication This will encourage Indian startups and industries to take an early lead in 5G

communication This will encourage Indian startups and industries to take an early lead in 5G technology. This testbed is first of its kind not only in Chhattisgarh but in Central India. IIIT-NR is now among the few premier institutions in India like IIT-Madras, IISc- Bangalore, IIT-Kanpur, IIT-Delhi, IIT-Hyderabad and SAMEER-Mumbai, which have their own 5G testbed. Big Data Computing Lab Objective: The purpose of the Big Data Computing Lab is to educate students in all aspects of large and distributed information systems (e.g. system development, testing, maintenance, data integration, networking, and application development) and, thus prepare them for highly emerging technologies in fast-growing IT industries such as Big Data computing, Health-care informatics, Data integration and Data analytics. Lab Facilities & Equipment: The research in the lab mainly focuses on next-generation data management and mining issues on BigData with special attention to heterogeneous information networks and social computing. An experimental setup for BigData analytics platform primarily using open source technologies such as Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS), MapReduce, YARN, Hive, MongoDB, Hbase, Apache Spark, MLlib, etc. Key Achievements:  Conducted workshop o Cyber security and blockchain technology, Nov 28-30, 2019  Ongoing project o Meity, Smart Agriculture for Tribes using Artificial Intelligence and Big Dataworth is 70 lakhs, 2020-2023 o SERB, Identification of Diseases in Millet Crop using Deep Learning for Next Generation Climate Smart Agriculture, 26 lakhs, 2019-2022 Page 5 of 8

Antenna and Microwave Circuit Design Lab Objective: The Microwave Lab supports intermediate and advanced courses in Electromagnetics and Microwave Engineering. Students experiment with transmission line propagation, antennas and microwave circuit components. Lab Facilities & Equipment: The microwave laboratories provide the necessary support for training the students in the area of RF and Microwave Engineering. It offers analysis and simulation of various components and devices to understand the basics of RF and microwave engineering, to boost the quality of engineering education, deepen understanding, and provide the necessary practical skills to young minds. The laboratory uses the following software and devices: Computer Simulation Technique (CST) Studio, Ansys HFSS, MATLAB, Vector Network Analyzer, Microwave signal generators, Antenna gain measurements, Waveguide and coaxial components of a wide variant and a anechoic chamber. IIIT-NR has truly world class, campus-wide state of the art information technology tools that are designed to meet the computing and communication needs of the institute, which has a fast, reliable and rugged computer network of more than 700 Nodes. In order to facilitate proper teaching aid, all classrooms here are equipped with projectors and audio systems and has two smart classrooms. All the hostels, cafeteria, academic block, guest house, multipurpose hall and residences, are connected through redundant 10 gigabit fiber backbone network. All the blocks are connected through layer 2 & 3 switches to provide 1Gbps connectivity at the user end. Wireless network with 84 indoor access points  to give total campus Wi-Fi coverage. All traffic for internet both inbound and outbound passes though 1+1 redundant UTM.

points to give total campus Wi-Fi coverage. All traffic for internet both inbound and outbound passes though 1+1 redundant UTM.

Internet Access: Through a 500 Mbps Internet leased line ( In ring Arctiticture), 1Gbps ( In ring Arctiticture) and  100 Mbps from NKN   with an  active–active configuration.   Internet connection range is provided through both LAN and Wi-Fi in all blocks inclusive of residences, academic, dinning and hostels.

Data Centre: IIIT-NR has a full-fledged data center of its own. It hosts 5 half blade form factor Inten XEON servers in a 16 slot chassis and has network unified storage of 35 TB. The datacentre is powered by redundant 100KVA UPS with N+1 backup.  All servers are connected to Internet by public IPs.

Virtual machines on cloud: -  The Institute has VMware Venter cluster perpetual licenses. VM cluster is formed with 1 Physical server failover configuration with total computation power of 80 CPU cores and 1TB of RAM.  All logical servers are created on top VM hypervisor which is managed by Venter server, this setup is a private cloud setup for IIIT-NR usage. Date of all virtual machines are kept at SAN and are backed up weekly using VMware EMC backup system.Institute also uses open source  ProxMox Hypervisor in cluster for one Xeon server dedicated for under grad students project.

Infrastructure Servers: - IT infrastructure uses servers for providing various important services to the institute. The servers are primarily all open source Linux based system. Severs like webserver, mail server, DHCP server, Active directory and internal DNS server. Public DNS server, helpdesk server, Library server, Moodle server, Oracle database server, and many more license server used for infrastructure of the institute. All the servers are created on VM cluster as mentioned above.

more license server used for infrastructure of the institute. All the servers are created on VM cluster as mentioned above.

Compute Server: - IT Department issues server infrastructure to students, faculty members to cater their computational needs on requirement basis. This is also issued from the VM cluster as mentioned above. Currently 2 computational servers have been issued to students and faculty to carry our research and project work. Apart for that One server with open source ProxMox Hypervisor in  dedicated for Under grad students project.

IP Telephony: Our entire Campus is equipped with IP telephony. It has 75 IP phones.

Video Conferencing: Polycom Real presence HD   VC System is available with multi party conference facility.

VPN: It can be used to access all IIIT-NR IT resources from outside campus using any Internet connection.

Software: Institute holds licenses on various software like Cisco WebEx,  VMware, Microsoft Office, Synopsys , Cadence , Ansys, Matlab , Netsim, Oracle, Wordsworth, CST etc. These are used by students, staff and faculty members. LabView,  Simulink, Orcad

Operating Systems and Services:- The institute mainly focuses on usage of free operating system like Ubuntu etc. But keeping in view of long term requirements, the institute also has licenses for Microsoft Windows MSDN dreams park account to upgrade/install their Microsoft products.

long term requirements, the institute also has licenses for Microsoft Windows MSDN dreams park account to upgrade/install their Microsoft products.

Desktop clients:-  The institute has 500desktops, 40 workstations at various labs and offices, 45 laptops and 70 printers and scanners. For labs institute has one server, 35 TB  Network unified storage dedicated for high end computing

Eclassroom :-  Institute has  two 120 sitters E-Classrooms. Equipped for two way (remote and IIIT-NR) interactive lectures. In this setup  16 simultaneous classrooms can be connected. Live streaming and recoding of lectures are being done using the Eclassroom Facility.

Institute library is part of the administrative building spanned over 2 floors acquiring plinth area of approximately 800 sq. meters with central air-conditioning system and open wi-fi.

Its primary aim is to:

Support the institute’s mission “To Create an Institute of Excellence in IT Education and Research for Meeting the Emerging and Challenging Needs of the Society.”

The mission and vision of Information Center is very closely based on the premises of Five Laws of Library Science propounded by renowned mathematician and father of library sciences Dr SR Ranganathan. These are:

of Five Laws of Library Science propounded by renowned mathematician and father of library sciences Dr SR Ranganathan. These are:

- Books/Information is for use. - Every reader his book/ information. - Every book/ information its reader. - Save the time of the reader. - Library is a growing organism. Collection Development:  We religiously follow the second and the third law when it comes to collection development. We go a step ahead when it comes to making available resources whether print or electronic by involving all the stake holders e.g, faculty members, students and researchers. It complements and supplements the scholarly and informational needs of faculty, students and researchers. Right from the day of inception it is aggressively building on its collection in varieties of forms like printed text books, reference books , magazines, newspapers and e resources like IEEE xplore, E-book collection of McGraw Hills etc. Digital Library section of the Central Library has developed an institutional digital repository using open source software DSpace, which preserve the institute's intellectual output for the posterity. Library has a separate section for books on history/flora & fauna of Chhattisgarh.

The Training & Placement Office at DSPM IIIT-Naya Raipur is concerned with every activity that enables students to learn and grow outside the Institute campus. On one hand, it collaborates with leading organizations and institutes in setting up internship and training program for the students while on other it enables the placement of students passing out from the Institute. The office liaises with prospective recruiters such as industrial establishments and corporate houses which conduct campus interviews and select students from both disciplines. It provides infra-structural facilities to conduct group discussions, tests, and interviews and other logistics required for the same.

Admission into the B. Tech programs of DSPM-IIIT Naya Raipur takes place through the Joint Entrance Examination (Main). Salient Features of Academic Curriculum:-

• Basic Motto: Skill First, Theory later, Project integrated

•Run with Fractal Academic concept, similar to IIT Hyderabad.

• Common syllabus for both CSE, ECE upto 4 semesters

• Project in every semester from 5th Semester.

• Eighth (8) semester dedicated for project work only.

• Students are allowed to continue the same project from 5th to 8th Semester to increase the depth or they can take up different projects in different domains to increase their breath.
heading_path: Training and Placement Cell Overview & Contacts

text:
Skill first

Click here for some interesting student projects

DSPM IIIT-Naya Raipur follows an innovative academic structure pioneered and first implemented by IIT-Hyderabad of fractal academics. This is considered as the first step towards experiential learning. At the center of Fractal Academics is the concept of T-concept of education – Breadth first and Depth next. A very similar concept is also being followed by IIT-Bhilai.

• Under this ‘T’ concept, course content is divided into two parts which require separate training. One part deals with the breadth of the topics and the other deals with depth of the concepts

• There can be more segments under each part dealing with either breadth or depth. Each segment is considered a fraction, thus it is said to be fractalized (divided) into various segments with 1 or 2 credits.

• Breadth courses are the basic building block for the depth courses.

• The fundamental idea is to atomize credits so as to enable the students to get a breadth of knowledge in more number of courses, however, deeper knowledge in the courses of their choice.

• Breadth courses are taught for first two years followed by depth courses for the remaining two years.

• Breadth courses are assigned 1 or 2 credits only. A number of such courses are offered to help build a broad perspective.

Theory Next

Depth courses are built on the foundation set by the breadth courses and are of 2 credits or more. Normally these are offered as elective courses. A student interested in pursuing a particular knowledge domain may opt for these courses.

Application Later

•Students are then required to work on mini/major projects to implement or understand the proof of concepts learned in depth courses.

IIIT-NR academics has several innovative features, which differentiates it from other similar institutes and helps students acquire skills necessary for their profession. Some of the salient features are:
heading_path: Key Advantages and Highlights of IIIT-NR

text:
it from other similar institutes and helps students acquire skills necessary for their profession. Some of the salient features are:

- Engineering courses right from First semester instead of 12th++ courses in First year - Skill First, Theory Later, Projects Integrated model for sound foundation of fundamentals - Fractal Academics with  short modular courses to enable inclusion of latest technologies in course curriculum - 'T'-Education model to enable students to acquire both breadth and depth of knowledge - Course curriculum judiciously designed to offer balanced exposure to both Hardware and Software with diverse set of tools (such as Arduino, Rasberry Pi, Sensor, RTL-SDR, Python, C, MATLAB, Cadence, Oracle etc.) for hands-on experience - Fosters project-based learning with FOUR mini projects, one each in 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th semester and ONE major project in 8th semester. A student can choose to do the same project from 5th to 8th semester for increased depth, or different projects for increased breadth - Elective subjects and multidisciplinary project options encourage students to develop interdisciplinary skills - Strong Industry-linkages for internships and industry-elective subjects in course curriculum
heading_path: Key Advantages and Highlights of IIIT-NR

text:
IIIT-NR has set up state-of-the-art labs with latest hardware and software tools in cutting edge technology areas. Some of these labs are:

- Data Science Lab - Antenna and Microwave Circuit Design Lab - Electronic Circuits Lab - Networks Design & Analysis Lab - Communication Systems Lab - VLSI & Embedded Systems Lab - Artificial Intelligence and Deep Leaning (AIDL) Lab - IOT & Sensors Lab
heading_path: Key Advantages and Highlights of IIIT-NR

text:
IIIT-NR offers a unique financial-aid facility to its students for international exposure. The key features are:

- Grant of up to Rs. Five Lakhs to 20 students from every batch for carrying out their final semester internship/project at a reputed Foreign University/Institute. - The project/work done is counted towards total credits of their formal education program
heading_path: Key Advantages and Highlights of IIIT-NR

text:
IIIT-NR fosters Research & Innovation and offers financial-aid to its students for pursuing research. The key features are:

- Encourages students by providing them financial support to participate in National/International Conferences, Seminars, Symposiums, Workshops to present their research work - Encourages students to publish their research work in journals and conferences - Provides financial support to students to prepare prototypes and for experimentation
heading_path: Key Advantages and Highlights of IIIT-NR

text:
IIIT-NR pays special attention to its students for their overall personality development. Some of the key initiatives towards this include:

- Nurtures a campus culture with high ethical standards - Institute extra-curricular activities are student driven to help students develop leadership, team spirit, sense of responsibility, time management, financial management, communication skill, inter-personal skill and many other soft skills, which are necessary for professional success - Student Activity Centre (SAC), consisting of various types of clubs, is completely managed by the students. SAC also conducts many extra-curricular activities. - Focussed on soft skills development, specially designed Workshops, Social Events and Invited talks are frequently organized - The institute helps students identify and pursue their PASSION
heading_path: Key Advantages and Highlights of IIIT-NR

text:
IIIT-NR encourages its students to participate in extracurricular activities and offers financial-aid to its students for participation in such events. The key features are:

- The institute has in-house facilities for sports and extracurricular activities - Encourages participation in outside competitions in both Team and Individual events/sports - Provides financial support of up to Rs. 10,000/- for participation in such events.
heading_path: Key Advantages and Highlights of IIIT-NR
